"rank-deficient lambda_max=1.0-2e-5 configs" (§277b) that I dismissed as artifacts WERE THE TRUE SUP being exhibited.
So: sup over ALL test functions = EXACTLY 1, approached on the zero-vanishing manifold. RH is NOT "<1 with margin" —
RH is "<= 1, never exceeded": an EQUALITY-SATURATED inequality with ZERO uniform slack. The 0.3-0.4 "margins" were
generic-basis artifacts (bases not tuned toward the saturation manifold). This retro-EXPLAINS the TP2 refutation (§289p):
near saturation there is no room for any stronger-than-PSD property — strengthenings MUST fail there (§289q, sharpened).
CONSEQUENCE: the extremal/saturating functions ENCODE THE ZEROS (f_hat vanishing at every gamma). Any exact certificate
must reproduce that zero-knowledge structurally — exactly what the Bondarenko-Radchenko-Seip Fourier-interpolation basis
(nodes at the zeros, §288b) formalizes. The certificate route and the saturation structure are the same object.
(C2) TP2 failure-window post-mortem (quantitative): §289p failure at w~1.1-1.7, recovery at w<=0.9 and w>=2. The window
brackets [1/log 3, 1/log 2] = [0.91, 1.44] — the PRIME-RESONANCE scales. Narrow-but-not-too-narrow functions resolve the
individual prime-2/3 oscillations cos(c log p), whose curvature flips the log-convexity sign. TP2 fails precisely in the
prime-2,3 resonance window. Clean mechanism; confirms the failure is structural, not numerical.
Corrections to NEXT_SESSION/map framing follow. LEDGER §290; Fable check on the night's keystone framing.


===== §291 — STORM #2: Transpose of Weil's ELEMENTARY (Castelnuovo-Severi) RH proof; the missing slot = arithmetic Riemann-Roch h^0; candidate = van der Geer-Schoof theta-h^0; our rank=N(band) is a dimension-count already (2026-07-25, Sam/Fable+Opus) =====
WEIL'S ELEMENTARY PROOF (function field, curve C/F_q genus g), step-by-step in template (§266-267) language:
 (W1) Surface S = C x C; cup product = intersection form on NS(S); Frobenius graph Gamma_F, diagonal Delta, fibers h,v.
 (W2) CASTELNUOVO-SEVERI inequality: for a correspondence T of bidegree (a,b), T.T <= 2ab; equivalently the intersection
      form on the 2-plane spanned by {h,v} inside NS(S) is hyperbolic, and Hodge-index => the ORTHOGONAL complement is
      NEGATIVE-DEFINITE. Apply to D = Gamma_F - (Gamma_F.v) h - (Gamma_F.h) v (Frobenius minus its fiber-degrees):
      D.h = D.v = 0 (D is primitive), so Hodge-index => D.D <= 0. Expand D.D using Gamma_F.Delta = #fixed points =
      #C(F_q) = q+1-Sum(alpha_i), Gamma_F.Gamma_F = q(2-2g), etc => Sum|alpha_i|^2 <= ... => |alpha_i|=sqrt q. RH.
 (W3) THE ENGINE under Castelnuovo-Severi = RIEMANN-ROCH on S: D.D <= 0 for primitive D comes from h^0(D)+h^0(K-D) and
      effectivity (h^0 >= 0). I.e. the negative-definiteness of the primitive intersection form = Riemann-Roch + h^0>=0.

flow) we have; the h^0-effectivity that powers Castelnuovo-Severi is the gap.

Riemann-Roch h^0(D)-h^0(K-D)=deg D+(1-g) (with the theta-smoothing built in, exact in their normalization). h^0>=0 is
STRUCTURAL (log of a positive theta sum). This is the arithmetic effectivity Castelnuovo-Severi needs.
OUR ASSET connects: §275 found rank(Weil form on a band) = N(band) = #zeros in band = a DIMENSION COUNT. The zeta zeros
are the "eigenvalues of Frobenius"; N(band) is the trace/count. So rank=N(band) is a candidate realization of the
arithmetic h^0 dimension count -- the Weil-form rank IS the h^0 of the relevant arithmetic divisor. (dim H^1 <-> zero count,
already the §266-267 template's cohomology-dimension slot.)

## §299 (2026-07-25) — FORWARD LEVER: the reality↔correspondence link probed as a generalized eigenproblem; the Weil form has a SPECTRAL GAP (difficulty is low-dimensional & localized to the de Branges subspace). REPORT (numerics), one verify-before-ship display-bug caught.

spectrum λ_i(P;A) GAP below 1 (difficulty localized to few directions) or ACCUMULATE at 1 (marginal everywhere)?

probes gave the same qualitative picture.)

  (all ≥0 to numerical zero). TWO eigenvalues ≈0 (−2e-14, 2.5e-7), then a jump to 0.0177 — a **spectral gap**.

  (RH-consistent, sup=1 saturation reached), TOP TWO ≈ 1, then GAP down to 0.505 and below (including NEGATIVE).

  the de Branges E / zero-vanishing direction (confirms §296). In it A(f)=P(f)=0.10296, P/A = 1.0 to 14 digits.

  (P(f)<0 ⇒ Q super-positive, big margin); only in the de Branges subspace does P rise to exactly meet A.

## §303 (2026-07-25) — first DIRECT CCM(|ζ|²)-vs-Weil form comparison + the CCM↔Weil ladder verified as an EXACT operator; the RH-hard step pinpointed as the LOG, not the derivative. REPORT + one exact verified identity.

operators/link_ccm_bridge.py — built the CCM positive form C[j,k]=∫F_jF_k·|ζ_trunc(½+ir)|²dr (≥0 by construction) and
the Weil form Q on the SAME band [14,38]/9 probes; first time both are put side by side numerically.
- **C eigs** all > 0 (min 0.0018) — positive-definite, as the |ζ|² measure must be. **Q eigs** = §300's (min −4e-16,
  RH-in-band holds). **R = C−Q is INDEFINITE** (eigs −5.3 … +0.40): the CCM positive form does NOT linearly bound the
  Weil form. Confirms §262 — the two live at different differential levels; there is no free linear positivity transfer.
- **EXACT verified identity (ratio = 1.000000 to 6 digits, all prime powers n=2,3,4,5,8,9):**
  **Λ(n)/√n = (log n / 2) · [Fourier coeff of log|ζ|² at freq log n]**  (log|ζ|² coeff at freq k·log p = (2/k)p^{−k/2}).
  This makes §262's qualitative |ζ|²→log→d/ds→ζ'/ζ ladder into an EXACT operator: the **Weil arithmetic form = the
  log-spectrum of the positive CCM measure, multiplied by ω/2** (ω=frequency; ×ω = derivative).

**Pinpointing the RH-hard step (honest, sharpens §262):** decompose the ladder |ζ|² → log|ζ|² → ×(ω/2) → Weil.
- The ×ω (derivative) step is NOT the villain: on the band ω=r>0, so ω·(positive weight) stays positive — multiplying a
  positive measure's weight by ω preserves positivity on the positive-frequency support.
- The **LOG step IS the villain**: log of a positive-definite measure is NOT positive-definite (log|ζ|² goes negative
  wherever |ζ|²<1). Positive-definiteness is generically DESTROYED by the log. RH ⟺ for ζ specifically, the ω-weighted
  log|ζ|² still induces a positive-definite (Weil) form. So the entire RH difficulty is concentrated in the transition
  from the measure |ζ|² (positivity free) to its logarithm log|ζ|² = the ζ'/ζ level — exactly the von Mangoldt step.

**Charisma:** the bridge identity = HANDLE (verified exact, 6 digits). The "log is the villain" decomposition = REPORT
(reasoned from the verified ladder + the sign of ω on the band). The C-vs-Q indefiniteness = HANDLE (measured).

**Honest significance:** the identity is essentially classical (Λ = −ζ'/ζ coefficients, log|ζ|² relation) — its value
is FRAMING: it converts the CCM↔Weil gap into one precise, classical operation (take the log of the positive |ζ|²
measure) and identifies that log as the sole locus where positive-definiteness can fail. Not new leverage, but the
sharpest, most explicit statement of WHERE RH lives that the CCM line has produced: RH = "log|ζ|² stays PD after ω/2."

**Next (loaded):** attack the LOG step directly — what structure in |ζ|² forces log|ζ|² to remain positive-definite

## §311 (2026-07-25) — DERIVED closed-form law for the Jensen hyperbolicity margin, verified: r_m ≈ −4u*(m)/(m(2u*+1)), u*~½log(m/π), from Φ's modular saddle. Matches exact to ~1-3%. The freshest genuine result of the session. HANDLE (derived + verified).

## §313 (2026-07-25, Fable) — EFFECTIVE GORZ: third-order saddle law derived+verified (sub-1%), Hermite hyperbolicity margins measured, explicit thresholds N(d) computed — degrees d=3,4 CLOSED for ALL n (within the leading-order scheme); d=5-8 finite checks running. **Motivation.** GORZ 2019 proves each degree-d Jensen polynomial J^{d,n} of the Ξ-moments is hyperbolic for all

closed-form margin law. §311 gave us one at 2nd order; this extends it to the order that controls degree d and builds
the explicit thresholds.

**(A) Third-order saddle law (operators/lp_thirdorder.py, dps 45, γ_m to m=24).** Exact implicit differentiation of the
saddle eq 2πe^{2u}=2m/u+9/2: u*' = 2u/D with D=2m(2u+1)+9u², u*'' = [2u'D−2uD']/D², D'=2(2u+1)+u'(4m+18u);
F'=2log u* ⟹ F''=2u'/u, F'''=2(u''u−u'²)/u²; then r_m = F''−4ψ'(2m+1), **c_m = F'''−8ψ''(2m+1)** (3rd log-difference
of γ_m). VERIFIED against exact central differences: c_m ratio saddle/exact = 0.80 (m=3) → 0.995 (m=12) → 1.0045
(m=22) — sub-1% for m≥12, BETTER convergence than the 2nd-order law. Magnitudes: c_m ≈ (1.1–1.2)/m² measured
(asymptote ~2/m² with log corrections; we use the conservative 2/m² in the scheme). c_m > 0, decaying — the cubic
deviation of log γ over a degree-d window is ≤ c·d³/6.

## §315 (2026-07-25, Fable) — THE TWO-CONSTANT RACE FLIPS: the directional (structured) Hermite margin decays POLYNOMIALLY, not geometrically — the effective-GORZ ladder is polynomial, N_dir(d) ≈ 1/√(3τ_d) ~ d²·const, vs the exponential worst-case ladder. (ratio ≈ 0.58 through d=20, §315 part 1). But the scheme's ACTUAL perturbation is structured: multiplicative
coeff_k → coeff_k·e^{t·g(k)}, g = the affine-reduced centered cubic (k−d/2)³−(3(d/2)²/4)(k−d/2), with t = c_n/6 > 0
ONE-SIGNED (c_m > 0 measured §313A). Legality: renormalization freedom absorbs affine-in-j and quadratic-in-j (X-scaling
and the Hermite-building δ); the centered cubic is pure odd ⟹ the reduced direction is exactly the residual. Measured
the DIRECTIONAL margin τ_d^+ = max t keeping He_d-perturbed hyperbolic:
  d=5..12: τ·d³ = 5.32, 2.42, 1.58, 1.20, 0.998, 0.875, 0.794, 0.740 — ratios rising to ~0.93 ⟹ POLYNOMIAL decay
  (τ ~ d^{−4±0.5}-ish; exact exponent from the rigorous run), NOT geometric. (d=4: unbounded ≥64 — small-d one-signed
  multiplicative perturbations can't break hyperbolicity at all.)
**Consequence:** the directional condition c_n/6 < τ_d ⟹ N_dir(d) = 1/√(3τ_d). At d=12: N_dir ≈ 28 vs worst-case
N_wc ≈ 534 — 19× smaller, and the gap grows exponentially. The effective ladder is POLYNOMIAL in d: coverage
n > N_dir(d) ~ C·d² for all d by one argument shape; the RH-difficulty on the Jensen front concentrates in the
polynomial corner n ≲ C·d² (the Ξ-like regime where the Hermite limit degrades), not the exponential bulk.

**Pólya-Schur placement (the conceptual finding).** e^{−tk²} coefficient multipliers are multiplier sequences
(Pólya-Schur 1914) — hyperbolicity-free; that IS the DBN heat-flow direction. The cubic exponent is the FIRST
non-multiplier direction (Σe^{tk³}x^k/k! has order >2, outside LP). So the c_m-cubic deviation is precisely the
leading term that NO heat-flow-type argument absorbs — the mathematical content of GORZ-uniformity beyond DBN, and
its per-degree tolerance τ_d (which Pólya-Schur does not quantify) is exactly what we measured. Honest: this is a
structural improvement of the effectiveness ladder + a sharp localization of the difficulty; it is NOT d→∞ uniformity
(the corner still grows). Next targets: (i) rigorous τ_d to d=20 (running), (ii) close all d with N_dir(d) ≤ our
107-moment reach (potentially d ≲ 25 same-day), (iii) the corner object J^{d,n}, n ≪ d² — its right limit is Ξ itself.

Ran the Roundtable-converged d*(T0) exchange-rate experiment (operators/dstar_experiment.py), pre-registered:
family Xi_T0 = Xi_xi·(1−z²/α²)(1−z²/ᾱ²), α=T0+i·1, one off-line pair at height T0; null d*∝T0².

1. All tested T0 < γ_1=14.13 — the pair is planted BELOW the first real zeta zero, a regime with no on-line zeros
   to "resolve against," where the GORTTW d~T² heuristic need not apply.

   (γ_{m−1}/γ_m ~ 40–90), the relative perturbation is (1/T0²)(2m)(2m−1)(γ_{m−1}/γ_m) = ORDER 1 even at m=1 for
   these T0 (e.g. T0=10,m=1: ~0.85). So the "planted pair" is a GROSS distortion, trivially caught at d=2 —
   not the small localized high-height violation the T² law is about.
The real regime (T0 ≫ 14, small localized pair) needs d* ~ T0² ≳ 200–2500, beyond the 131 cached moments AND into
degree-hundreds polyroots (unstable — cf. §319 NoConvergence at d=120). This is EXACTLY Red's pre-registered failure
mode #3 ("if d*∝T0², a T0 span 3→30 chases first failures to degree ~900, precision collapses near the LP boundary").

law in its actual regime is a real compute investment (moments to m~300–600 via Φ-quadrature + a stable high-degree
hyperbolicity test, e.g. Sturm/Hankel-signature instead of polyroots), NOT a quick probe. Deferred, not concluded.

Arithmetic content is an invariant of the BULK (symbol/potential/measure), not the boundary condition; boundary tuning moves ≤n levels, it cannot manufacture the prime-driven S(T). APPLICATION to xp/archimedean-prolate Hilbert–Pólya: the archimedean operator is 1D Sturm–Liouville ⇒ F_0=O(1) arithmetic-free (§467b), deficiency (2,2) ⇒ ≤2 shift (§467), S(T) unbounded ⇒ NO extension reproduces S(T) (categorical, explains the empirical §466 NULL). CONSTRUCTIVE CONSEQUENCE: S(T)=−(1/π)Σ_p Σ_k p^{−k/2}sin(kT log p)/k is prime content ⇒ must enter through the BULK = the CCM semilocal measure dm_S=|∏_v L_v(½−is)|²ds (§465), not a boundary condition; the delicate extension that matters is the SEMILOCAL operator's (primes already inside), = §451-457 off-diagonal coupling analytic-side. Full writeup: RH_NOGO_extension_arithmetic.md. STATUS: rigorous general core (rank-≤n bound + Corollary); rigorous CCM-specific (§424/425 Arb, §467b S-L); empirical horn (3 instruments). My §471 decomposition split ξ'/ξ = A'/A (A=ξ/ζ, "triv") + ζ'/ζ ("arith"). I read the near-total cancellation |λ_arith|/λ_triv→1 as a third encoding of the a=1 razor edge. ## §769 — The single-Gaussian Weil curve D(a): scaling reduction + rigorous grazing map

Three linked probes (verify-before-ship throughout; float bug caught + fixed en route).

**(1) Scaling of the Weil-form min-eigenvalue** (`operators/weil_mineig_scaling.py`).
Built a fast float Weil-form builder, Ω(r) precomputed once (basis-independent).
**Bug caught + fixed:** first version summed over primes p only, omitting prime POWERS (von Mangoldt
Λ(n)=log p for n=p^k) — diagonal off by 0.03–0.5, oscillating sign, spuriously pushing a=35 negative
(contradicted the rigorous §767 PD cert — the contradiction is what flagged it). After the von-Mangoldt
fix the float diagonal for {15,25,35,45} matches the rigorous Arb {1.48591,3.14122,0.04810,0.19167}
to 1e-5. Then a grid-cutoff artifact (R=120<a=125) faked a −0.79 min-eig at N=12; fixed with R=240.
**Clean result:** (A) well-separated basis (Δa=10): Weil form is ≈ DIAGONAL (Gaussian-cosine test
functions at separated freqs are ≈Weil-orthogonal), min-eig = smallest diagonal, stable +0.048. (B)
dense basis in a fixed window: min-eig decreases 0.048→0⁺ as density grows (Gram degeneracy) — the form
is positive but **NOT coercive** (inf=0), matching the known analytic structure. No genuine negative
eigenvalue anywhere once artifacts removed (RH-consistent).

**(2) Reduction.** On the separated family, positivity ⟺ every DIAGONAL entry
`D(a)=arch(a)+pole(a)−prime(a) > 0` — the single-Gaussian Weil functional W(φ_a),
φ_a(x)=e^{−x²/2}cos(ax) (Bombieri–Lagarias). D(a)>0 ∀a is a NECESSARY condition for RH.

**(3) Rigorous grazing map** (`weil_diagonal_curve.py` float sweep + `weil_diagonal_rigorous.py` Arb).
Float sweep: D(a)≈0 to machine-eps for a below the first zero (14.13), then D>0 above. This is the
EXPLICIT FORMULA showing itself: D(a)=Σ_γ h_a(γ), a positive zero-sum; below the first zero φ_a
overlaps no zeros so D grazes 0; above, D traces zero contributions. Float can't resolve the sign in
the grazing zone (±1e-15). **Arb certification (prec 300):**
- D(a) **≥ 0 CERTIFIED** for a ∈ {8,10,12,13,14,15,20}: D(8)=+1.42e-16, D(10)=+1.18e-7,
  D(12)=+0.033, D(14)=+3.085 — growing super-exponentially toward the first zero.
- a=3: D∈[−4.3e-22,+9.8e-21]; a=5: D∈[−7.7e-21,+2.6e-21] — **|D|<1e-20, sign NOT certified** at this
  precision (below the integration-error floor).

**REPORT:** single-Gaussian Weil positivity is rigorously CERTIFIED for a≥8; it is razor-thin
(0<D<1e-16) approaching the first zero from below, and sub-resolution (|D|<1e-20) further down. This
**localizes RH's hard core quantitatively** (concretizes §749's 3-way cancellation): positivity is

grazing regime is where any positivity PROOF must do its work. **No Handle for RH:** this is a

## §771 — CORRECTION to §770: the identity DOES hold — it's QUADRATIC (sum of squares over zeros)

§770 retracted §769's "D(a)=zero-sum" claim after testing D against the LINEAR sum 2Σφ̂_a(γ). That was
the wrong test. The correct identity is the QUADRATIC one (the Weil form is Q_{jk}=Σ_ρ φ̂_j(γ_ρ)φ̂_k(γ_ρ),
so the diagonal is a sum of SQUARES):

   **D(a) = arch(a,a)+pole(a,a)−prime(a,a) = Σ_ρ φ̂_a((ρ−½)/i)² = 2 Σ_{γ>0} φ̂_a(γ)²**

Verified (`weil_diagonal_curve.py` + zeros10k) against the rigorous Arb D(a), ratio ≈ 1 to 4 digits:
  a=8: 1.4208e-16/1.420e-16=1.0006 · a=10: 1.1816e-7/1.180e-7=1.0014 · a=12: 3.2965e-2/3.296e-2=1.0001
  a=13: 1.0000 · a=14: 1.0000 · a=15: 0.9999 · a=20: 1.0003. (Residuals = finite-10k-zero truncation.)
So §769's interpretation was RIGHT and §770's retraction was itself the error — corrected here.

**Why this is the clean RH statement.** φ̂_a(r)=√(2π)/2(e^{−(r−a)²/2}+e^{−(r+a)²/2}). D(a) is computed
from the ARITHMETIC side (digamma integral + pole + von Mangoldt primes) WITHOUT assuming RH, yet it
equals Σ_ρ φ̂_a((ρ−½)/i)². IF all ρ are on the line (γ real), each term is (real)² ⇒ D(a)≥0 manifestly.
If some ρ were OFF the line (ρ=β+iγ, β≠½), that term is φ̂_a(γ−i(β−½))² — φ̂_a of a COMPLEX argument,
whose square can be negative/complex and could drive D(a)<0. Hence **D(a)≥0 is exactly the single-test-
function Weil positivity, and it grazes 0 below the first zero because φ̂_a(γ)² is exp-small when a sits
below every γ** (§769's shape, now with the correct closed form).

**Standing rigorous facts:** D(a)≥0 CERTIFIED (Arb) for a≥8 (down to +1.42e-16 at a=8); below that the
SOS value 2Σφ̂_a(γ)² is genuinely positive but < Arb's ~1e-21 resolution. The scaling reduction +
non-coercivity (§769) stand. **No Handle for RH:** this is the Weil criterion restated as a verified
identity on one test-function family; proving D(a)≥0 for ALL a from the arithmetic side alone (no zeros)
is RH — still open. But the sum-of-squares structure is now the exact, verified target. Net this
session: several self-caught errors (von-Mangoldt, grid artifact, §770 wrong-sum) — discipline holding.

## §772 — The organ-2 Weil form IS a GRAM matrix of zero-evaluation vectors (verified, unifying)

Generalized §771's diagonal identity to the full matrix and VERIFIED it to machine precision
(`operators/weil_gram_identity.py`):

   **Q_{jk} = arch(a_j,a_k)+pole−prime  =  2 Σ_{γ>0} φ̂_{a_j}(γ) φ̂_{a_k}(γ)  =  ⟨v_j, v_k⟩**,
   v_j := (√2 · φ̂_{a_j}(γ))_{γ>0},  φ̂_a(r)=√(2π)/2(e^{−(r−a)²/2}+e^{−(r+a)²/2}).

Arithmetic side (primes + digamma integral, no zeros) vs Gram side (from zeros10k), max abs diff:
  close {14,15,16,17}: 2.9e-15,  Gram rank 1/4  (all 4 sample the single zero 14.13 → min-eig 0)
  dense [20,24]/5:     4.7e-15,  Gram rank 2/5
  separated {15,25,35,45}: 5.3e-15, Gram rank 4/4 (full) → min-eig +0.04810
Machine-precision agreement in EVERY case, full-rank and rank-deficient alike.

**This unifies §769 completely.** The scaling behavior is now explained, not just observed:
- separated a_j ⇒ the vectors v_j sample DISJOINT sets of zeros ⇒ nearly orthogonal ⇒ Q≈diagonal,
  min-eig = smallest ‖v_j‖² (the smallest diagonal, +0.048).
- dense/close a_j ⇒ the v_j all sample the SAME few zeros ⇒ nearly linearly dependent ⇒ Q
  rank-deficient ⇒ min-eig → 0⁺. The non-coercivity (§769) is Gram rank-deficiency.

**The clean RH statement (rigorous, standard Guinand–Weil structure — verified here on the apparatus):**
Q is computed from the ARITHMETIC side with NO assumption on zero locations, yet equals ⟨v_j,v_k⟩ with
v_j real IFF every γ is real. So **Q PosSemidef for all bases ⟺ {v_j} are real vectors ⟺ all γ∈ℝ ⟺ RH.**
An off-line zero ρ=β+iγ (β≠½) injects φ̂_a(γ−i(β−½)) — a COMPLEX coordinate — turning Q into a Gram
matrix under a bilinear (not positive) form, which can fail PSD. The whole difficulty of RH-via-Weil is
proving, from primes+digamma alone, that this matrix has the Gram-of-REAL-vectors structure.

**REPORT:** end-to-end verification that our organ-2 Weil apparatus computes exactly the Guinand–Weil
Gram matrix of the zeros (confirms §731/§757/§767 certificates are the genuine object, and explains

is non-coercive (min-eig→0⁺ as basis densifies); Arb certification needs min-eig(Q) > ρ (enclosure
floor ~1e-11, §757). Mapped min-eig vs basis density in three windows:
  [15,55]: certifiable to N=11 (spacing 4.0, min-eig 3.3e-9); N=12 (sp 3.64) min-eig → 2.7e-15 (cliff).
  [15,45]: certifiable to N=8  (spacing 4.29, min-eig 3.9e-3); N=9  (sp 3.75) → 3.0e-15.
  [20,40]: certifiable to N=6  (spacing 4.0, min-eig 7.3e-3); N=7  (sp 3.33) → 2.1e-15.
The collapse is a CLIFF (1e-3 → 1e-15 in one refinement step), not gradual.

**The edge = the mean zero spacing.** At window center T, mean zero spacing = 2π/log(T/2π):
  [15,55] T=35: zero-spacing 3.658 — edge in [3.64,4.0] ✓

SAME zeros ⇒ V rank-deficient ⇒ min-eig collapses to the numerical floor. A Nyquist/sampling threshold.

**REPORT:** the practical frontier of finite Weil verification is the zero-density Nyquist scale; the
"hardest" test-function directions (near-null of Q) are those resolving individual zeros at that scale.
Any proof of full (all-test-function) Weil positivity must control exactly this critical-resolution

## §779 — Tested (and refuted) a midpoint-factorization reduction; sharpens why diagonal ≠ sufficient

Fresh proof idea, tested before banking. Large-a,b, the Weil kernel approximately FACTORS:
  K(a,b) = arch+pole−prime ≈ e^{−(a−b)²/4} · D((a+b)/2),
a Gaussian in (a−b) times the single-Gaussian curve D (§769/§771) at the midpoint (the diagonal
K(a,a)≈D(a) recovers §769). IF `g(a−b)·h((a+b)/2)` were PD whenever `h≥0`, then 2-variable Weil
positivity would reduce to the 1-variable D(a)≥0 — a real lever. **Tested the claim numerically
(`h`-sweep, 25-pt basis): FALSE.** min-eig of the kernel matrix:
  h=1 (const): +0.126 (PD) · h=smooth bump: +2e-4 (PD) · h=1+cos(m): **−0.052** · h=|sin 2m|: **−0.70**
  · h=cos²(m): **−0.15** · h=1+0.99cos(3m): **−0.97**.
So `h≥0` does NOT imply the kernel is PD — fast-oscillating nonneg `h` break it. Reduction refuted;
no false lever banked (verify-before-ship).

**Sharpening (the value):** this concretely shows WHY single-Gaussian positivity D(a)≥0 is NECESSARY
but NOT SUFFICIENT for the full Weil form (matching §772's off-diagonals-matter). The full form is PD
not because D≥0, but because the TRUE D(m)=2Σφ̂_m(γ)² is **PD-compatible** (slowly varying — a smoothed
zero-density) — and it is slowly-varying/PD-compatible precisely BECAUSE the zeros are real (RH). An
off-line zero would inject fast/complex oscillation into D, of exactly the kind that breaks kernel PD.
So RH ⟺ "D is PD-compatible," a strictly stronger condition than D≥0. **No Handle for RH:** another
angle honestly reduced to RH-completeness (every reduction on this family does — the criterion has no
hidden shortcut here). Net: the diagonal/off-diagonal split is now understood as ≥0 vs
PD-compatibility, and the latter is the RH-content.

## §786 — Operator-lane frontier map (deep-read: Suzuki 2606.09096 + Kim 2607.24830)

Deep-read of the two current papers, to map exactly where the Weil-positivity/operator approach to RH
stands (Aug 2026) and what the wall is.

**Suzuki 2606.09096 — PROVEN:** operator A_a = Friedrichs extension of B_a = D*G_a D, with G_a the integral
operator whose kernel is the SCREW FUNCTION g(t) (explicitly containing the prime sum Σ_{n≤e^|t|}
Λ(n)/√n(|t|−log n)). Thm 1.1: A_a self-adjoint. Eq 1.1: its quadratic form EQUALS the Weil form,
Q_W^a(v)=⟨A_a v,v⟩. Thm 1.5: zeros of W(a,θ;z) are real. All WITHOUT assuming RH.
**Suzuki — OPEN (the gap to RH):** Corollary 1.6 — IF one can choose θ=θ(a) and φ(a,z) with
lim_{a→∞} e^{φ(a,z)} W(a,θ;z) = z²ξ(½−iz)/ξ'(½−iz) uniformly on compacts, THEN RH. Proving this limit
(eq 1.12) "as an identity of complex functions" gives RH; Suzuki: it is "expected to require a detailed
analysis of the arithmetic contribution coming from the PRIME terms."

**Kim et al 2607.24830 — numerically realized it + found the wall.** Archimedean law (R1)
λ_k(a)=log(1/a)+log(k−½)+B₀+O(a), B₀=log q−2log2, universal (R2, Dirichlet + modular forms), 30-digit;
off-line detection (R6, rate 2δ); zero-sum reconstruction corr 0.9915. **R4d KEY: "primes act DIAGONALLY
on the archimedean basis" — median diagonal 1.55 vs off-diagonal 1.3e-14** (= my §769/§772 "Weil form ≈
diagonal on separated basis", also a rediscovery). **R8 THE WALL (they call it fundamental, not a
discretization artifact):** W is a Paley–Wiener transform of exp-type a ⇒ zero density a/π (→∞); the target
z²ξ/ξ' has density log T/2π. Corollary 1.6's θ(a) must cancel a density-a/π zero set down to log T/2π —
"we did not find such a θ(a)." The zeros live in the SYMBOL-LEVEL ERROR TERM, not the eigenvalues (R4d:
"direct spectral GUE detection is impossible at finite a"). Their verdict: "the converse — bounded ⇒
on-line, i.e. proving boundedness unconditionally — is RH itself and is closed to us. No finite
computation and no easy argument can cross that wall."

**Synthesis / what this means for us.** (1) My independent apparatus converged on the SAME crux they and
Suzuki name — the prime/arithmetic contribution's resummation (§732/§749) — which is real cross-validation
that the crux is correctly located. (2) Essentially all of my §769–784 (arch universality, primes-diagonal,
off-line detection, Nyquist/Paley–Wiener density) is in Kim (§785). (3) The precise OPEN problem of the
lane is now: **Suzuki's Corollary 1.6 — construct/characterize θ(a) making W(a,θ;z)→z²ξ/ξ' uniformly,
i.e. thin the exp-type-a zero set (density a/π) to the target (density log T/2π) as a→∞.** This is the
loaded frontier; it is genuinely hard analytic NT (prime-term control), and the best current work reaches
it and stops. Not a wall for the endeavor — a precisely stated open problem, now understood at the level
of the state of the art. No Handle for RH.

## §787 — Generalized the Bessel contribution to arbitrary integer order (besselJ_pos), for mathlib

Acting on the §786 conclusion (stop grinding the walled proof lane, work the genuine Lean edge). Kim/Suzuki
own the proof frontier; our genuine asymmetric asset is the verified-formalization loop. mathlib has NO
Bessel functions at all — so strengthened the extracted contribution (`mathlib_contribution/BesselJ01.lean`)
from J₀/J₁-specific to GENERAL integer order:
- `besselJ (n : ℕ) (x) = ∑ₖ (-1)^k/(k!(k+n)!)(x/2)^{2k+n}`.
- **`besselJ_pos`**: `0 < J_n(x)` for `0<x`, `x² < 4(n+1)` — via the alternating-series bound
  `J_n(x) ≥ (x/2)ⁿ/n!·(1−(x/2)²/(n+1))`. **Unifies** the two hand-proved cases (J₀ on x²<4, J₁ on x²<8)
  into one theorem over all orders. Verified through verify_loop (PASS, trusted axioms only).
- `besselJ0_eq`, `besselJ1_eq`: the specific defs ARE `besselJ 0`, `besselJ 1` (subsumption).
Full file compiles clean against pinned mathlib (trusted kernel axioms only). This is the genuinely novel,
non-reproduction output of the day: a general-order Bessel positivity theorem in Lean, exploiting the
verification edge rather than competing on analytic NT where the field is walled. Contribution is now
materially stronger for a mathlib PR (general J_n, the design a reviewer would want). Submission still
gated on Jacob's Zulip/CLA (§ prior). No Handle for RH.

## §843 (★ the floor coefficient is the EXACT constant 1/(2π) — the budget side of the race is GROUNDED, essentially provable ★) — operators/floor_constant_check.py
The §842 floor law was fitted (0.144–0.182·ln(t/2π)). Tested whether the leading coefficient is the EXACT
constant 1/(2π)=0.159155. Computed floor(t) at t=80..4020 (length-40 window, 4W=3):
  floor/[(1/2π)ln(t/2π)] = 0.886, 0.973, 0.991, 0.998, 0.9992  → 1 cleanly and monotonically.
  floor ≈ (1/2π)·Ω̄(window) even tighter: 0.886→0.9992 (Ω̄ = window-mean of Ω(t)=Re ψ₀(¼+it/2)−lnπ).
⟹ floor(t) → (1/2π)·ln(t/2π) EXACTLY (coefficient 1/(2π), NOT a fit). And more precisely floor ≈ (1/2π)·Ω̄(window).
WHY THIS IS ESSENTIALLY PROVABLE (Szegő-type): the archimedean operator is multiplication by (1/2π)Ω(t)
compressed to band-limited functions concentrated on the window [a,b]. The min eigenvalue of a smooth-multiplier
(Toeplitz-like) operator → the symbol's window-minimum: floor → (1/2π)·min_{[a,b]}Ω. Since Ω(t)~ln(t/2π) is
increasing + slowly varying over a fixed-length window, min_window Ω = Ω(a) ≈ Ω̄ ≈ ln(t/2π). So
floor(t) → (1/2π)ln(t/2π), unconditionally (standard symbol-min asymptotic, no RH input).
SIGNIFICANCE: the BUDGET (archimedean floor) side of the arch-vs-prime race is now GROUNDED in an exact
constant and an essentially-provable asymptotic — not an empirical fit. Half the race is characterized
unconditionally. (Caveat: at LOW height the convergence isn't reached — floor(t=29)=0.125 is BELOW the
asymptotic (1/2π)Ω̄~0.24, because the min eigenvalue picks up window-edge/curvature at low t; that low-corner
deficit is exactly why the hard corner is hard — the floor there is smaller than its own asymptotic budget.)
THE RACE, now sharp: floor(t) = (1/2π)·min_window Ω [budget, exact/provable] vs pnorm(4W) [prime obstruction,
empirical ~(4W)^0.71]. RH at the corner ⟺ pnorm(4W) stays below the (small, low-height) floor as 4W→∞. NEXT:
ground the PRIME side too — is pnorm(4W) similarly a symbol-max or a prime-sum quantity with an exact constant?
If BOTH sides get exact symbols, the race becomes an explicit inequality (arch symbol-min vs prime symbol-max).

## §844 (the Weil form IS a compressed multiplication operator; positivity is NEVER pointwise — always from the band-limiting lift = the RH-hard object, precisely located) — operators/weil_symbol_check.py
Following §843 (arch floor = symbol-min of (1/2π)Ω): tested whether the WHOLE Weil form is a compressed
multiplication operator with symbol S(r) = (1/2π)Ω(r) − P(r), where P(r) = (1/π)Σ_{log n<4W}Λ(n)/√n cos(log n·r)
is the prime oscillation (straight from the explicit formula). CONFIRMED:
  margin ≥ min_window S(r) in ALL cases (Rayleigh bound for a compressed multiplication operator) ✓
  BUT S_min < 0 EVERYWHERE: [14,44] S_min=−0.41(4W=2),−0.32(3),−0.66(4); [100,130]−0.55,−0.65; [400,430]−0.56.
  arch symbol-min 0.13–0.66 vs prime symbol-MAX 0.68–1.23 — the prime oscillation ALWAYS locally exceeds the
  arch budget, so min S < 0 always. The pointwise sufficient condition "min S ≥ 0" is NEVER satisfied.
⟹ Weil positivity is NEVER pointwise-symbol positivity — it is ALWAYS produced by the BAND-LIMITING LIFT: the
margin is raised from the (always negative) symbol-min (~−0.5) up to the actual positive margin (+0.1 … +1e-9)
purely because band-limited test functions can't concentrate at the symbol's negative min (their
positive-definiteness averages the oscillation out). This is the standard Weil-criterion structure (positivity
from test-function positive-definiteness, not pointwise), faithfully reproduced by our apparatus.
NET: §843+§844 ground the RACE in explicit-formula symbols — arch symbol (1/2π)Ω(r) [exact, §843] vs prime
oscillation P(r)=(1/π)ΣΛ/√n cos(log n·r) [explicit-formula exact]. The margin = symbol-min + LIFT. The

positive-definiteness gain), = the §834 non-scalar protection, now precisely located as an
uncertainty-principle quantity: how much does band-limiting raise λmin above the essential-range min of an

## §854 (CORRECT resolution of the §853 basis question — the margin is SUBSPACE-INTRINSIC (basis-independent); the razor is intrinsic to the band-limited subspace, NOT a basis artifact) — conceptual
§853 asked "is the razor a Fejér-basis artifact?" and ran a flawed Gaussian probe. The question is answered
CORRECTLY without any probe, and §853's framing was conceptually confused:
KEY FACT: margin = λmin(Q, G) = min over the SPAN of Q(φ)/‖φ‖² (a generalized eigenvalue). This is a property of
the SUBSPACE, not the basis within it — ANY two bases spanning the same subspace give the IDENTICAL margin
(generalized-eigenvalue basis-invariance). So there is no "Fejér-basis artifact" to escape: every band-limited
basis of the same span yields the same margin.
⟹ The razor-thinness is INTRINSIC to the band-limited (Paley-Wiener) test-function SUBSPACE at the given capacity
— it is NOT a basis choice. The §853 Gaussian "basis" was not a different basis for the same problem: Gaussians
span a DIFFERENT function space (not band-limited), which changes the Weil-positivity problem itself (and breaks
the finite-exact prime sum). So the Gaussian comparison was ILL-POSED, not merely approximate — corrected here.
CONSEQUENCE: the "try a better basis to dodge the razor" hope is mathematically void. The razor lives in the
band-limited subspace intrinsically; the RH-critical near-null modes (§850-851) are subspace-intrinsic directions;
RH ⟺ they stay ≥0. Changing the test-function SPACE (Gaussian/Hermite, à la CCM) is a genuinely different problem
(CCM's program), not a reparametrization of ours — worth pursuing as CCM's own setup, but it does NOT make our
razor "go away." Honest correction of §853 (verify-before-ship: caught the conceptual error, not just the numeric one).

## §858 (★ WHAT the RH-critical near-null mode IS: it vanishes at the in-window zeros; its positivity comes ENTIRELY from tails hitting the OUT-of-window zeros — the Nyquist mechanism, concrete ★) — operators/nearnull_which_zeros.py
Shifted to the ZERO SIDE (validated): Q_zero(v)=2Σ_γ F_v(γ)² (test function F_v=Σv_c F_c evaluated AT the real
zero heights — a MANIFEST sum of squares, no complex-FT trap). Extracted the margin eigenvector at [14,44], 4W=4.8,
N=15 (margin 8.5e-11). Explicit-formula check: Q_zero(vmin)=6.3e-11 ≈ margin ✓ (zero side = prime+arch side).
FINDING (clean, mechanistic): the RH-critical near-null mode VANISHES at all 8 IN-WINDOW zeros — they contribute
0.0% of the residual. Its entire tiny Weil value comes from TAILS hitting the OUT-of-window zeros: 60.83 (18.2%),
52.97 (16.4%), 79.34 (14.6%), 84.74 (8.6%), 92.49, 87.43, 48.01, ... — each 2·F_v(γ)² > 0.
MECHANISM (concrete Nyquist/sampling): a band-limited function of capacity N can interpolate ZERO at the #zeros
in-window zeros (that's what makes it near-null, §850: near-null dim = N−#zeros), but its tails NECESSARILY hit
the neighboring out-of-window zeros (band-limited ⇒ not compactly supported), and those tail contributions —
2·F_v(γ)², a sum of squares over the REAL zero heights — keep Q > 0. So the RH-marginal positivity at the corner
is secured by the mode's INABILITY to also vanish at the surrounding zeros.
WHY IT'S MANIFESTLY ≥0 = WHY IT'S RH: Q_zero = 2Σ_γ F_v(γ)² is a sum of squares BECAUSE the zeros γ are REAL
(on the line) ⇒ F_v(γ) real ⇒ each term ≥0. An OFF-LINE zero ⇒ F_v(complex height) ⇒ term not manifestly ≥0 ⇒
positivity could break. So the manifest sum-of-squares positivity IS "zeros are real" = RH — our apparatus computes
Q from the prime+arch side (no zeros) and gets ≥0 precisely because, by the explicit formula, it equals this real
sum of squares. This is the cleanest "what IS the RH-critical mode" answer of the run — the zero-side lens (§858
path-check shift) gave it; earlier eigenvector probes (§835/846/855) couldn't because they used the wrong lens.
Ties together §832 (razor at N=#zeros), §850 (near-null dim=N−#zeros), §856 (t*=1 at corner).

whose small-prime arch/prime balance is exactly critical (arch=prime), residual positivity from uncaptured-zero

## §862 (★ THE CLEANEST "WHY" — Szegő: Weil positivity holds because the symbol has POSITIVE MEAN (arch mean>0, prime oscillation mean=0) and band-limited functions see the AVERAGE; the razor is where band-limiting resolves the local dips ★) — operators/szego_spectrum.py
Compared the FULL Weil eigenvalue distribution to the symbol S(r)=(1/2π)Ω(r)−P(r) distribution over [50,80] 4W=3,
N=8/13/18 (below→over capacity):
  eig MEAN 0.354/0.373/0.372 ≈ symbol MEAN 0.378 (trace identity ✓); eig MEDIAN ≈ symbol median (0.38).
  BUT symbol ranges [−0.572,+1.262] with 25% NEGATIVE, while ALL eigenvalues POSITIVE (min 0.091→0.0005→0.0 as
  N→cap, never <0). The eigenvalues are the symbol PULLED TOWARD ITS MEAN — extreme symbol values (negative dips
  AND positive peaks) averaged out by the band-limiting.
THE MECHANISM (cleanest "why Weil positivity holds" of the run):
  1. The symbol S = (1/2π)Ω − P has POSITIVE MEAN. arch mean ≈ (1/2π)⟨Ω⟩ = floor ~ (1/2π)ln(t/2π) > 0 (§843);
     the PRIME oscillation P=(1/π)ΣΛ/√n cos(log n·r) has ZERO MEAN over the window (⟨cos(u r)⟩ ~ 1/(u·width) ≈ 0).
     So mean S ≈ arch mean > 0 — the prime side does NOT lower the average, it only makes LOCAL dips.
  2. Band-limited test functions see the symbol's AVERAGE (Szegő trace), which is positive ⟹ Q > 0.
  3. The razor (margin→0) is where band-limiting starts to RESOLVE the symbol's local negative dips (as capacity
     is approached). FULL resolution (Szegő limit N→∞, 25% of eigenvalues going negative) lies OUTSIDE the valid
     BAND-LIMITED Weil regime (that limit = the raw multiplication operator, not band-limited test functions).
CONSEQUENCE: Weil positivity is "almost trivial" (positive mean, prime averages out) YET subtle (RH = whether
band-limited functions of ANY type ever RESOLVE a net-negative dip where the prime locally beats the arch). This
is the crux made vivid. UNIFIES the whole run: §843 (arch mean=floor>0), §844 (symbol negative locally), §858/859
(band-limited resolution/sampling), §850 (razor at capacity), §856 (t*=1 at corner), §860/861 (small primes make
the dips). The cleanest single mechanistic statement of why Q≥0 holds and why proving it uniformly is RH.

## §863 (Szegő fluctuation CULMINATION — RH ⟺ the min-eigenvalue downward fluctuation from the mean never exceeds the mean; saturated (=0⁺) at the razor) — operators/szego_fluctuation.py
Tested whether (mean_S − min_eig)/std_S is bounded by a universal C < mean/std (which would give a FREE sufficient
condition mean_S > C·std_S). Result across 6 windows × 3 capacity-fractions:
  At frac=0.95 (near capacity): (mean−min_eig)/std → mean/std EXACTLY (min_eig→0): 0.788=0.788, 0.601=0.601,
    0.831=0.831, 0.805=0.805, 1.003≈1.163 — the fluctuation SATURATES at mean/std at the razor.
  At frac=0.5 (below capacity): ratio SUB-critical (0.20–0.60 < mean/std) → genuine positivity margin.
INTERPRETATION (clean, honest): the min eigenvalue's downward fluctuation from the symbol mean is AT MOST mean/std
(in std units) — i.e. min_eig ≥ mean_S − (mean_S/std_S)·std_S = 0. So "the fluctuation is bounded by the mean" IS
min_eig ≥ 0 = RH, restated. And it is SATURATED (=exactly mean/std, min_eig=0⁺) at critical sampling = the razor.
So RH ⟺ the min-eigenvalue downward fluctuation NEVER OVERSHOOTS the mean. The free-sufficient-condition hope
(universal C < mean/std) is REFUTED: the fluctuation reaches exactly the mean at criticality (that's the RH-marginal
knife-edge). BUT below capacity it's strictly sub-critical → quantifies WHY the certified below-capacity positivity
(§830/§849) is robust (the fluctuation hasn't reached the mean yet), and pins RH as precisely the critical limit.
CULMINATION of the §858–862 mechanism: symbol mean>0 (arch mean=floor, prime osc mean=0, §862); band-limited fns
see the mean (Szegő); the fluctuation below the mean is sub-critical below capacity (positivity margin) and
saturates the mean at the razor (min_eig=0⁺). RH = the fluctuation never overshoots. This is the cleanest complete
mechanistic account of the run — why Q≥0 holds (positive mean), why there's a razor (fluctuation→mean at critical
sampling), and why proving it uniformly is RH (the saturation is exactly marginal, no slack to exploit).

## §864 (the §862/863 mechanism IS Szegő-Widom / Landau-Widom extreme-eigenvalue theory — a PROVEN framework; but it confirms the min-eig → symbol min in the unrestricted limit, so positivity = the band-limited restriction = RH; same wall, now in proven language) — WebSearch [REPORT]
Checked whether the §862/863 Szegő-fluctuation picture connects to a proven framework. It does — WebSearch (REPORT
tier, not deep-read) confirms the relevant proven theory:

  Wiener-Hopf / Toeplitz operators.
- Parter-Widom: main-term asymptotics for the EXTREME (min/max) eigenvalues of Toeplitz matrices.
- "Toeplitz/Bargmann-Toeplitz operators with symbols of VARIABLE SIGN" — spectrum governed by the geometry of the
  positive/negative parts of the symbol (exactly our sign-changing S).
- Landau-Widom: eigenvalue distribution of time-and-frequency limiting = prolate spheroidal (our band-limiting).
CONNECTION (honest): our compressed multiplication-by-S operator IS a truncated Toeplitz/Wiener-Hopf-type operator;
§862/863's mechanism (eigenvalues distribute like S, min-eig → symbol min as N→cap, band-limiting lifts below cap)
is precisely Szegő-Widom/Parter-Widom/Landau-Widom extreme-eigenvalue theory. So the §862/863 picture sits in a
DEEP PROVEN FRAMEWORK.
BUT (same wall, confirmed a 6th way): Parter-Widom PROVES the min eigenvalue → symbol MIN (negative, ~−0.5) as
N→∞ for a fixed window — but that unrestricted limit is the OVER-capacity/non-band-limited regime, OUTSIDE the
valid Weil (band-limited, finite exponential type) regime. The theory describes the razor's structure beautifully

on the band-limited/finite-type RESTRICTION keeping min-eig ≥ 0 uniformly, which is exactly RH. Szegő-Widom gives
the eigenvalue asymptotics but NOT an unconditional positivity bound for the restricted (band-limited) operator.
NET: the mechanism is now placed in its proven home (Szegő-Widom/Landau-Widom), a real gain in understanding — and
it re-confirms (6th independent framing) that proving uniform positivity of the band-limited restriction is RH.
NEXT (deeper, if pursued): read Parter-Widom / Landau-Widom for whether their finite-N (band-limited) extreme-eig
bounds — not the N→∞ limit — give anything unconditional for our specific symbol. REPORT-tier until deep-read.

## §866 (★ DID the derivation — the finite-N Szegő bound rigorously reduces to Beurling-Selberg (§847); the matched band-limit=prime-cutoff is WHY there is no slack (§863 explained); unifies the two frameworks ★) — analytic derivation
Attempted the §865 target (derive a finite-N min-eig lower bound for the compressed arch−prime operator). It resolves
cleanly and connects everything:
DERIVATION: min-eig = min over band-limited φ (type 2W, on window) of ∫S(r)|φ(r)|²dr/‖φ‖², S=(1/2π)Ω−P.
  1. φ type 2W ⟹ |φ|² band-limited to 4W, |φ|²≥0, ∫|φ|²=‖φ‖². So ∫S|φ|² = ∫S_{≤4W}|φ|² (only S's ≤4W part couples).
  2. The prime oscillation P=(1/π)Σ_{log n<4W}Λ(n)/√n cos(log n r) has ALL frequencies {log n} < 4W ⟹ P ⊂ S_{≤4W}:
     the band-limiting SMOOTHS NOTHING (prime cutoff = 4W = the |φ|² band exactly). So min-eig ≥ min_window S_{≤4W}
     = min S < 0 — the soft bound is EXACTLY USELESS.
  3. ⟹ THE MATCHED BAND-LIMIT (2W→|φ|² band 4W) = PRIME CUTOFF (log n<4W) IS WHY THERE IS NO SLACK. This DERIVES
     §863's "fluctuation saturates the mean, no slack": the two cutoffs coincide by construction, so no smoothing
     gap exists to exploit.
  4. The ONLY improvement over min S: use the constraint g=|φ|² ≥ 0 (positive-definite / Fejér-positive spectrum).
     min ∫Sg over {g≥0, band-4W, ∫g=1} > min S iff S has a positive band-limited minorant with positive integral —
     which is EXACTLY the BEURLING-SELBERG extremal problem (§847).
CONCLUSION: the finite-N Szegő-Widom derivation (§864/865) RIGOROUSLY REDUCES to the Beurling-Selberg problem for
our symbol S (§847) — the two frameworks are the SAME wall via this derivation. §847 established Beurling-Selberg
gives only RH-conditional bounds for our S (the extremal minorant stays negative). So this path, worked out
rigorously, lands exactly on the known wall — but now with a PRECISE STRUCTURAL REASON for the no-slack (matched
band-limit/prime-cutoff) and a clean unification of the Szegő-Widom, Beurling-Selberg, and §862/863 fluctuation
pictures. THIS is how the search resolves: attempt the derivation → it either gives slack or reduces to the wall;
here it reduces (matched cutoffs), and the derivation itself is the honest, rigorous result. The genuinely-new
result would need a positive band-limited minorant of S with positive integral (unconditional) — which, given the
matched cutoff, requires the g≥0 constraint to do ALL the work, i.e. a Fejér-Riesz/Bochner positivity of the
arch−prime symbol that doesn't route through the zeros = the "new positivity mechanism" (still the open core = RH).

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
§897  THE ARCHIMEDEAN DENSITY IS CAUCHY–STIELTJES (unconditional, from digamma) — pointwise origin of Groskin's TP tail
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
HANDLE (operators/omega_cs.py) + analytic derivation. From ψ₀(¼+ir/2)=−γ+Σ_n[1/(n+1)−1/(n+¼+ir/2)]:
    Ω(r) = Re ψ₀(¼+ir/2) − ln π = −γ − ln π + Σ_{n≥0} [ 1/(n+1) − a_n/(a_n² + r²/4) ],   a_n = n+¼.
Each r-dependent term is −a_n/(a_n²+x/4) with x=r² — a Cauchy–Stieltjes kernel in x. Hence
    dΩ/dx = Σ_n (a_n/4)/(a_n²+x/4)²  is COMPLETELY MONOTONE (sum of CM functions).
VERIFIED: (1) the series matches the direct digamma Ω to ~4e-6 (series-truncation residual) at r=0.5..150; (2) the
finite-difference signs of dΩ/dx and its x-derivatives are (+,−,+,−) at every x∈{1,9,100,2000,20000} — the CM pattern.
⇒ Ω(r) is a Bernstein-type function of r² with a Stieltjes (CM) derivative = the archimedean density is Cauchy–Stieltjes,
UNCONDITIONALLY, straight from the digamma series. By Bernstein's theorem dΩ/dx = ∫₀^∞ e^{−xs}dρ(s), ρ≥0. CONSEQUENCE:
the archimedean quadratic form arch(φ)=∫φ(r)²Ω(r)/2π dr is a POSITIVE combination of resolvent forms ∫φ²/(a_n²+r²/4) —
manifestly positive, and this is the pointwise/analytic realization of Groskin T3.2's totally-positive Cauchy–Stieltjes
archimedean tail (§895). This is a real, provable structural handle on the ARCH side (the explicit, non-prime side of
the scalar criterion §891). OPEN LEVER (the genuine next theory step): use the resolvent/CS representation of arch to
bound arch − prime BELOW — i.e. bound the single-negative-eigenvalue depth μ (§889-891) via the resolvent structure vs
the prime oscillation P(r)=(1/π)ΣΛ(n)/√n cos(r log n). That bound, if it dominates the pole-coverage p(v·w)², is RH.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
§897b  CORRECTION to §897 (verify-before-ship): CM is of the DERIVATIVE; arch is NOT pointwise-positive
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
§897 overstated one line. SOLID & VERIFIED: dΩ/d(r²) is completely monotone (signs +,−,+,− confirmed), so Ω(r) is
concave-increasing in r² with a Cauchy–Stieltjes (CM) derivative — an unconditional structural fact from the digamma
series. WRONG in §897: "arch is a manifestly positive combination of resolvent forms." Ω(r) itself is NEGATIVE at
small r (Ω(0.5)=−3.33, Ω(3)=−0.74; it crosses 0 near r≈11 and floor=mean Ω/2π>0 only on average) — so the arch
quadratic form's positivity STILL relies on band-limiting (φ can't concentrate at small r), exactly like the full
symbol σ. The CM/CS property is a genuine handle on the SHAPE of Ω (monotone-concave in r², resolvent-decomposable
derivative), NOT a manifest-positivity proof of arch. Net: the arch side is "nontrivially positive" too (band-limited),
which means the §897 lever is subtler than stated — the resolvent structure constrains Ω's shape but doesn't trivially
dominate the prime oscillation. Honest status of the lever: promising for controlling Ω's variation, not a positivity
shortcut. (This is the same self-correction discipline as §888/§889 — caught on my own re-examination before shipping.)

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
§898  CLOSED-FORM archimedean weight + the u=2π crossing scale (frequency-domain arch-vs-prime, Guinand–Weil frame)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
HANDLE (analytic + operators/freq_compare.py, freq_verify.py). Cosine-transformed the archimedean density into the
Guinand–Weil frequency frame. Each Lorentzian a_n/(a_n²+r²/4) → π e^{−2a_n|u|}; geometric sum over a_n=n+¼ gives the
CLOSED FORM archimedean weight (full-line cosine transform of Ω):
    Ŵ(u) = −π e^{u/2}/sinh(u) = −2π e^{u/2}/(e^u − e^{−u}).
CONFIRMED numerically: transforming the FULL Ω with convergence factor e^{−εr}, the numeric/closed ratio is EXACTLY
2.0 and CONSTANT across u=log2..3 (2.0 = one-sided vs full-line convention; the shape −e^{u/2}/sinh u matches perfectly).
u→0: Ŵ ~ −π/u (the ln-singularity of Ω); u→∞: Ŵ ~ −2π e^{−u/2} → 0.
THE COMPARISON: |Ŵ(log n)| = 2π n^{3/2}/(n²−1) ≈ 2π/√n vs prime mass Λ(n)/√n = log n/√n. RATIO = 2π / log n.
  ⇒ the archimedean weight POINTWISE-DOMINATES the prime masses for log n < 2π (n < e^{2π} ≈ 535, u < 2π ≈ 6.283),
    and the primes exceed the arch weight only for u > 2π. THE CROSSING SCALE IS u = 2π — exactly the t/2π scale of the
    Weil formula. Consistent with §890: extra negative eigenvalues turn on as bandwidth 4W crosses 2π≈6.28 (seen at
    4W=5–7). For 4W=4 < 2π the arch weight pointwise-dominates the whole band (ratio ≥ 2π/4 ≈ 1.57 > 1).
HONEST CAVEAT: this is a POINTWISE-in-frequency comparison; the true arch form is a CONVOLUTION (Toeplitz with kernel
Ŵ), not diagonal, so pointwise domination does NOT rigorously give operator domination (same subtlety as §886/§888 —
the tiny negative eigenvalue at 4W=4 capacity is an off-diagonal effect). But the u=2π crossing is a genuine structural
scale and the closed-form Ŵ(u)=−π e^{u/2}/sinh u is a clean, verified, unconditional handle on the arch side.
NEXT: the operator comparison — is the Toeplitz(Ŵ) form ⪰ the prime point-mass form on the band? and does 4W<2π give a
provable pointwise-to-operator domination (arch weight dominating with room to spare below the 2π crossing)?

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
HANDLE (operators/ratio_probe.py). Quantified the scalar-inequality slack π_w/μ (π_w=p(v·w)² pole coverage, μ=defect
depth) across 25 well-conditioned corners (#neg=1, G PD; windows [14,44],[14,34],[20,50],[30,60]; 4W=3,4,5; frac 0.6-0.8):

    gets EASIER above the corner (μ→0 faster than pole coverage). The razor (ratio→1) is a LOW-HEIGHT phenomenon.
READ: the scalar inequality π_w ≥ μ (§891) has genuine but THIN slack (~3% at the razor), concentrated at low height;
it does NOT approach 1 arbitrarily in this sweep (min 1.027). THE CRUX for a proof: is there a UNIFORM positive floor
π_w/μ ≥ 1+δ (δ~0.02-0.03), or does the ratio →1 at critical sampling (frac→1) / deeper corners? A uniform floor,
proven, IS RH; ratio→1 would mean the razor is asymptotically zero-slack. Not settled here (frac≤0.8) — the next
make-or-break test is frac→1 at the low-height corner, watching whether the ~3% floor holds or thins. This is the
sharpest quantitative statement yet of exactly how much room the RH-corner inequality has.

## §1035 — Abstract Tate canonical height + Néron–Tate positivity SKELETON  [Handle, EXIT0]
File: ~/rhforge/forge/TateHeight.lean (Olympus). Self-contained real-analysis construction of the
canonical (Néron–Tate) height — the input I'd called "years away" 3 ticks earlier, built in ONE session.
Given h:X->R, T:X->X, d>1, and |h(Tx) - d*h x| <= C:
 • canht x := h x + ∑' k (seq(k+1)-seq k) where seq n = h(T^[n]x)/d^n (Tate telescoping limit).
 • incr_bound / geo_summable / incr_summable: increments bounded by C/d^(k+1), summable (geometric).
 • seq_tendsto: seq n -> canht x (the limit exists).
 • canht_functional: canht(T x) = d * canht x (d-homogeneity).
 • canht_sub_le: |canht x - h x| <= C/(d-1).
 • canht_iterate: canht(T^[n]x) = d^n * canht x.
 • canht_zero_orbit_finite (THE POSITIVITY HEART): given Northcott (∀B, {y|h y<=B}.Finite), canht x=0 =>
   forward T-orbit {T^[n]x} finite. For T=doubling on an elliptic curve: zero canonical height => torsion
   = Néron–Tate positivity, the exact input arithB/§1023 consumes.

## INSIGHT (2026-08-17) — ℝ-nondegeneracy of the regulator is NOT a separate deep input: it follows
## from NORTHCOTT (§1052, already proven) + Dirichlet approximation (elementary).
The apparent second remaining gap (regulator det>0 / ĥ pos-def over ℝ) was thought to need the deep
classical "NT nondegenerate" theorem. But: suppose the regulator Gram form Q (PSD, §1073) is DEGENERATE,
i.e. ∃ real v≠0 with Q(v)=0. Q PSD ⟹ (Cauchy–Schwarz) the polar B_Q(·,v)=0 and Q(w−tv)=Q(w) ∀t∈ℝ,w
(Q is constant along the radical direction v). By Dirichlet/pigeonhole on the torus ℝⁿ/ℤⁿ, the line ℝv
has INFINITELY MANY lattice points w∈ℤⁿ within bounded distance C, so Q(w)=Q(w−tv)≤C'‖w−tv‖²≤C'' bounded
for infinitely many DISTINCT integer combos ∑wᵢPᵢ (distinct for independent Pᵢ). But Q(w)=ĥ(∑wᵢPᵢ), so
{P : ĥ P ≤ C''} is INFINITE — contradicting Northcott (§1052 finite_naiveHeight_le). ⟹ Q nondegenerate ⟹
pos-def over ℝ. So the regulator ℝ-pos-def ⟸ (Northcott ✓ + points ℤ-independent + n-dim Dirichlet).
n-dim Dirichlet ("∞ many lattice points within bounded dist of a line") is ELEMENTARY (compactness of
ℝⁿ/ℤⁿ + pigeonhole), NOT deep. Mathlib has 1-D Dirichlet (NumberTheory/DiophantineApproximation/Basic:
exists_int_int_abs_mul_sub_le, infinite_rat_abs_sub_lt_one_div_den_sq_of_irrational). NET: the ONLY truly
deep remaining classical input is WEAK MORDELL–WEIL (E(K)/2E(K) finite). Nondegeneracy is now a
build-it target, not a wall. NEXT ATTACK: formalize posDef_of_posSemidef_of_lattice_northcott.

## §2077 (2026-09-06 01:47 CDT) — WeilHalfBoundSufficient.lean — half_bound_guarantees_psd

**Result:** For diagonal `a,b,c > 0` and cross-terms `d,e,f` satisfying `d² ≤ ab/4`, `e² ≤ ac/4`,
`f² ≤ bc/4` (each within HALF its own pairwise Weil bound), the full 3×3 Gram determinant
`abc − af² − be² − cd² + 2def` is automatically `≥ 0` — realizable/PSD — **regardless of the signs**
of `d,e,f`.

**Why it matters:** §2070 (`WeilPairwiseInsufficient.lean`) showed that cross-terms sitting *exactly*
at their pairwise Weil bounds can, under an adversarial sign combination, force a negative Gram
determinant — i.e. pairwise bounds alone are insufficient for joint realizability. That result left
open exactly how close to the boundary the danger zone actually is. §2077 answers it precisely: HALF.
Below half the bound, sign can't matter at all; the §2070 pathology is confined to the outer half of
the allowed range.

**Proof chain (no sorry):**
1. `a·f² ≤ abc/4`, `b·e² ≤ abc/4`, `c·d² ≤ abc/4` — multiply each bound by the opposite diagonal entry.
2. `(def)² ≤ (abc/8)²` — multiply all three bounds together: `d²e²f² ≤ (ab/4)(ac/4)(bc/4) = (abc/8)²`.
3. Take `Real.sqrt` of both sides of (2), `Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs` on each side, `abs_of_nonneg` on
   `abc/8`, then `abs_le.mp` to extract `−(abc/8) ≤ def`.
4. `nlinarith` closes: `abc − (af²+be²+cd²) + 2def ≥ abc − 3·(abc/4) − abc/4 = 0`.

Compiled on Olympus (`~/rhforge/forge/WeilHalfBoundSufficient.lean`), `.olean` built.
`#print axioms half_bound_guarantees_psd` → `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`. EXIT0, zero sorry.

**Lesson:** first attempt used a `Real.sqrt`-heavy `nlinarith` one-shot with `sq_nonneg` cross terms —
failed (`linarith failed to find a contradiction`, `sorryAx` in the axiom list confirming the gap).
Rewritten as an explicit multi-step chain (bound each square term individually, bound the triple
product via `mul_le_mul` composition, extract the signed lower bound via the `Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs` +
`abs_le` pattern already proven reliable in §2075) — compiled clean on the second attempt. Reinforces
the standing lesson: `nlinarith` with sqrt-adjacent hints is unreliable for anything beyond 2-variable
Cauchy–Schwarz; explicit algebraic decomposition into named `have` steps is the dependable path for
3-variable-or-more inequality chains.

## §2078 (2026-09-06 01:49 CDT) — WeilHalfBoundTight.lean — half-bound threshold is TIGHT

**Result:** Answers the sharpening question §2077 left open, using §2070's OWN extremal configuration
directly (`a,b,c=2,8,32`; extremal `d,e,f=4,8,-16` giving `det=-2048<0`). Scaling that exact adversarial
sign pattern by a factor `x∈[0,1]` (`d,e,f = 4x, 8x, -16x`), the Gram determinant is `512(1−3x²−2x³)`.
- At `x=1` (full extremal, §2070's original): `det=-2048` ✓ matches.
- At `x=1/2` — exactly the boundary where §2077's hypothesis `d²≤ab/4` saturates with equality
  (`d²=4=ab/4`) — `det=0` exactly. §2077's guaranteed lower bound is *achieved*, not slack.
- At `x=3/5` — hypothesis now violated (`d²=5.76>ab/4=4`) — `det=512(1-1.08-0.432)=-262.144<0`,
  reproducing §2070's pathology.

**Why it matters:** confirms "half" is not an arbitrary conservative margin picked because it happened
to work — for this genuinely adversarial configuration it is the EXACT crossing point between realizable
(`det≥0`) and impossible (`det<0`). §2077's theorem is sharp: no weaker hypothesis (allowing any
`x>1/2` uniformly across all sign patterns) could give the same unconditional guarantee, because this
specific configuration breaks immediately past `x=1/2`.

**Proof:** four `norm_num` closed numeric facts — no algebraic machinery needed since every value is a
concrete rational: (1) hypothesis saturation check, (2) determinant `=0` at `x=1/2`, (3) determinant
`<0` at `x=3/5`, (4) hypothesis violation check at `x=3/5` (so (3) isn't a counterexample to §2077 — the
hypothesis was never satisfied there).

## §2079 (2026-09-06 01:55 CDT) — WeilExtremalFactorization.lean — the general explanation for §2078's tightness

**Result:** §2078 checked one numeric configuration (`a,b,c=2,8,32`) and observed the Gram determinant,
scaled by `x` along the extremal 2-positive-1-negative sign pattern, factors as `abc(1−2x)(x+1)²`. This
brick proves that factorization is a UNIVERSAL ALGEBRAIC IDENTITY, not a coincidence of that one
instance: for `d = x√(ab)`, `e = x√(ac)`, `f = −x√(bc)` (the extremal cross-terms at scale `x`, for ANY
`a,b,c > 0`), the Gram determinant `abc − af² − be² − cd² + 2def` equals EXACTLY `abc·(1−2x)·(x+1)²`.

**Consequence (`symmetric_extremal_nonneg_iff_x_le_half`):** since `(x+1)² ≥ 0` unconditionally and
`abc > 0`, the sign of the determinant is exactly the sign of `(1−2x)` — nonnegative if and only if
`x ≤ 1/2`, for every positive diagonal triple, not just §2078's specific numbers. This is the structural
REASON the half-bound threshold (§2077) is tight (§2078): it isn't an artifact of one adversarial
configuration, it's baked into the algebra of the extremal sign pattern itself.

**Sanity check:** `general_formula_matches_2070_instance` plugs in `a,b,c=2,8,32, x=1` and recovers
`-2048` exactly, matching §2070's original hand-computed extremal determinant — confirms the general
formula specializes correctly to the concrete case that started this whole thread.

**Proof:** `symmetric_extremal_det_formula` — expand `(x√(pq))² = x²pq` via `Real.sq_sqrt`, and the
triple product `√(ab)√(ac)√(bc) = abc` via two applications of `Real.sqrt_mul` collapsing to
`√((abc)²) = abc` via `Real.sqrt_sq`; substitute and close with `ring`. `symmetric_extremal_nonneg_iff_
x_le_half` — direct case split: forward via `mul_neg_of_pos_of_neg` contradiction, reverse via
`mul_nonneg` composition, both closed by `nlinarith`.

expression had `2 * (x*√ab) * (x*√ac) * -(x*√bc)` as one associated term but the prepared rewrite lemma
`e4` covered only `(x*√ab) * (x*√ac) * -(x*√bc)` (missing the leading `2 *` factor), so the pattern
literally wasn't present in the goal to rewrite. Fixed by writing `e4`'s LHS to match the goal's exact
subterm INCLUDING the `2 *` prefix, then folding the `2` into the RHS constant. General reminder:
`rw` needs syntactic (up to defeq) subterm match, not just mathematical equivalence — when a rewrite
target isn't found, check exactly how the surrounding goal parenthesizes/associates the term, not just
whether the equation is true.

## §2080 (2026-09-06 01:59 CDT) — WeilBalancedVsFrustrated.lean — the combinatorial explanation

**Result:** proves the companion to §2079's frustrated-pattern formula. With all three extremal
cross-terms sharing the SAME sign (`d=e=f = x√(ab), x√(ac), x√(bc)` all positive — a "balanced" 3-cycle,
sign-product `(+1)(+1)(+1)=+1`), the Gram determinant is `abc·(1−x)²·(1+2x)` — a DIFFERENT cubic from
§2079's frustrated form `abc·(1−2x)·(x+1)²` (sign-product `(+1)(+1)(−1)=−1`).

**The dichotomy:** the balanced form is nonnegative for EVERY `x∈[0,1]`, touching zero only at the full
bound `x=1` (generalizing §2070's specific numeric `consistent_sign_choice_gives_zero_not_negative` to
every `a,b,c>0`, not just one instance). The frustrated form already goes negative past `x=1/2` — a
strictly earlier, strictly interior failure point. `balanced_and_frustrated_disagree_at_full_bound`
confirms concretely: at `x=1`, balanced gives exactly `0`, frustrated gives `-4abc` (strictly negative)
— genuinely different functions, not the same fact restated.

**Why it matters:** this is the graph-theoretic explanation for the whole §2070/§2077/§2078/§2079 thread.
A 3-cycle of cross-term signs is "balanced" (product of the three pairwise signs `=+1`) or "frustrated"
(product `=−1`) — exactly the physics/graph-theory notion of a frustrated triangle in an Ising/spin-glass
sense. Balanced sign patterns are structurally safe all the way to the naive full pairwise bound;
frustrated patterns are the ONLY ones capable of breaking realizability strictly inside that bound
(specifically at the halfway point, per §2079's exact factorization). This turns "why does sign matter"
(§2070's original open question) into a clean, checkable combinatorial criterion, not just case-by-case
numerics.

**Proof:** identical algebraic skeleton to §2079 (`Real.sq_sqrt`, `Real.sqrt_mul`/`Real.sqrt_sq` for the
triple product, `ring` to close) with the single sign flip in the cross-term product — confirms the two
formulas are genuinely twin results, differing only in that one sign. `balanced_pattern_nonneg_on_unit_
interval` closed by `positivity` directly once the two nonneg factors were established.

## §2081 (2026-09-06 02:03 CDT) — WeilFourVarSharedFrustration.lean — the first genuine 4-variable (K4) result

**Result:** the first result in this arc to genuinely scale past 3 variables. With 4 diagonal entries

4×4 Gram determinant computes to `5x⁴ − 6x² + 1`, which factors as `(x²−1)(5x²−1)`. On `x∈[0,1)`, this is
nonnegative iff `x² ≤ 1/5` — breaking down at `x = 1/√5 ≈ 0.447`, STRICTLY EARLIER than the
single-triangle threshold `x=1/2` (`shared_frustration_strictly_earlier`: `1/5 < 1/4`).

**Why it matters:** shows the balanced/frustrated dichotomy (§2080) generalizes in the expected
direction but with genuinely richer content: two frustrated triangles sharing an edge don't just
independently reproduce the single-triangle threshold — they COMPOUND, breaking realizability strictly
earlier. This is the first concrete evidence that the "how many/which triangles are frustrated"
combinatorics (Harary signed-graph balance theory) actually controls the *severity*, not just the
presence, of the realizability breakdown — exactly the richer structure predicted when moving from K3
(one triangle, no choice) to K4 (four triangles, many possible frustration patterns).

**Proof technique — genuinely different from the sqrt-heavy §2077-§2080 proofs:** chose all-diagonal-1
so no `Real.sqrt` bookkeeping was needed (with `a=b=c=d=1`, cross-terms are already the plain scalars
`±x` — no square-root normalization required). Computed the determinant symbolically via Mathlib's own
`Matrix.det_succ_row_zero` cofactor-expansion + `Matrix.det_fin_three` for the resulting minors + `ring`
— the same reliable pattern §2064 established for 4×4 determinants (offloading the correctness of the
24-term expansion to Mathlib rather than hand-deriving it). Sign characterization via `mul_neg_of_neg_
of_pos` (forward) and `mul_nonneg` (reverse) case analysis, both closed by `nlinarith`.

## §2082 (2026-09-06 02:07 CDT) — WeilFourVarAllFrustrated.lean — the trend continues, confirmed monotone

**Result:** tests whether the threshold keeps dropping with richer frustration. Sympy pre-check (before
any Lean) of two candidate variants — (A) two DISJOINT edges flipped `(1,2)` and `(3,4)`, (B) two edges
sharing a vertex flipped `(1,3)` and `(1,4)` — found variant B gives the IDENTICAL polynomial to §2081
(`5x⁴-6x²+1`), while variant A gives a genuinely new polynomial `-3x⁴-8x³-6x²+1 = -(x+1)³(3x-1)`.

**Why B matches §2081 exactly:** not a coincidence — signed-graph "switching"/gauge equivalence. Flipping
all edges incident to one vertex (`s_i → -s_i` for a single vertex) conjugates the sign matrix by
`diag(s)`, which preserves eigenvalues/determinant. Variant B's two negative edges sharing vertex 1 are
reachable from §2081's single negative edge by exactly this kind of gauge move, so they're the SAME
underlying frustration structure in disguise — only variant A (disjoint edges, not reducible by any
single vertex flip) is genuinely new.

**Variant A result:** the two-disjoint-edges pattern makes ALL FOUR of K4's triangles frustrated
simultaneously (every triangle contains exactly one of the two flipped edges). Determinant factors as
`-(x+1)³(3x-1)`; since `(x+1)³>0` for `x>-1`, realizability (`det≥0`) holds iff `x≤1/3` — STRICTLY
smaller than §2081's `x²≤1/5` threshold, confirmed via `all_frustrated_strictly_lower_than_shared`:
`(1/3)²=1/9 < 1/5` (compared via squares to avoid touching `Real.sqrt`, fully rigorous since both
thresholds are positive).

**The confirmed trend:** single frustrated triangle (n=3, §2077-§2080, breaks at `x=1/2`) → shared-edge
double-frustration (n=4, §2081, breaks at `x=1/√5≈0.447`) → all-four-triangles frustrated (n=4, §2082,
breaks at `x=1/3≈0.333`). More genuine (gauge-inequivalent) frustration monotonically lowers the
realizability threshold — now demonstrated across three genuinely distinct combinatorial structures, not
just two data points.

the determinant; `nlinarith` case split for the sign characterization).

subterm needs.

## §2083 (2026-09-06 02:11 CDT) — WeilGaugeInvariance.lean — the general gauge-invariance principle

**Result:** formalizes the explanation invoked informally in §2082 for why a "2 edges sharing a vertex"
K4 sign pattern gave the exact same determinant as §2081's "1 edge flipped" pattern. `gauge_flip_
preserves_det`: for ANY `n`, ANY matrix `M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ`, and ANY sign vector `s : Fin n →
ℝ` with every `s_i ∈ {1,-1}`, the "gauge-flipped" matrix with entries `s_i·s_j·M_ij` has EXACTLY the same
determinant as `M`. This is the formal statement of signed-graph "switching equivalence" (a standard
tool in Harary/Zaslavsky signed-graph theory): conjugating by a `±1` diagonal matrix is an orthogonal
similarity transform, which cannot change the determinant, since `det(diag(s))² = (∏s_i)² = 1`
regardless of the actual signs.

**Why it matters:** turns an ad-hoc observation ("these two determinants happened to match") into a
certified structural fact with a genuine proof, and — more importantly for the rest of this arc — gives
a real, reusable TOOL: before spending a full determinant computation (sympy + Lean) on a new K_n sign
pattern, first check whether it's reachable from an already-computed pattern via a vertex-sign flip; if
so, its determinant (and hence its realizability threshold) is already known for free. This will save
real effort in any future K5/K6 exploration of this vein.

**Proof:** the gauge-flipped matrix equals `diag(s) * M * diag(s)` as a matrix product (`ext` +
`Matrix.mul_apply`/`Matrix.diagonal_apply` + `simp`), then `Matrix.det_mul` (applied twice) plus
`Matrix.det_diagonal` reduces the goal to `(∏s_i) · det(M) · (∏s_i) = det(M)`, closed via
`(∏s_i)² = 1` (itself from `∏(s_i·s_i) = ∏1 = 1`, using `s_i²=1` for `s_i=±1`).

Compiled on Olympus (`~/rhforge/forge/WeilGaugeInvariance.lean`), `.olean` built. Both theorems:
`#print axioms` → `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`. EXIT0, zero sorry.

**Lesson:** first compile attempt failed on `rw [Matrix.det_mul, Matrix.det_mul, Matrix.det_diagonal,
Matrix.det_diagonal]` — the SECOND `Matrix.det_diagonal` had no remaining occurrence to rewrite, because
Lean's `rw` rewrites ALL syntactically-identical occurrences of a matched pattern in ONE application, not
just the first — since both `diag(s)` instances in the goal were literally the same term `s`, the single
`rw [Matrix.det_diagonal]` call closed both simultaneously. General reminder: `rw [lemma, lemma]`
(repeating the same lemma name) is only needed when the two occurrences differ in their metavariable
instantiation; if they're syntactically identical, one application suffices and a second use of the same
lemma will error "did not find an occurrence."

collateral frustration from an identical LOCAL change, purely because the graph got denser. Sympy
pre-check gave the 5×5 Gram determinant (diagonal all-`1`, one edge flipped to `-x`) as
`-8x⁵+9x⁴+8x³-10x²+1 = -(x-1)²(x+1)(8x²-x-1)`.

**The rational witness (avoiding irrational roots entirely):** `x=3/7` lies safely inside §2081's K4
single-edge-flip safe region (`(3/7)²=9/49 < 1/5`) yet makes K5's determinant strictly negative
(`k5_unrealizable_at_three_sevenths`, verified by `norm_num`). Same relative perturbation `x`, same
"single edge flipped" structure — but K5 is already broken while K4 is still fine. This isolates DENSITY
itself (not just "more triangles are frustrated," which was §2081/§2082's finding) as an independent
factor tightening the threshold.

**Genuine tooling obstacle overcome:** the reliable 4×4 recipe from §2064/§2081/§2082
(`simp [Fin.sum_univ_four, Matrix.det_fin_three, Matrix.submatrix_apply, Fin.succAbove]; ring`) does NOT
scale to 5×5 — two consecutive attempts (`simp only` with an expanded lemma set, then adding explicit
`cons_val`/`head_cons` lemmas) both left a huge unresolved mess of nested `if`-`then`-`else` Fin-index
terms that `ring` could not close, because concrete numeral Fin indices (like the literal `2` in
`![...] 2`) weren't being reduced to their underlying `cons_val` chain by the *restricted* `simp only`
lemma set. FIX: use plain `simp [...]` (NOT `simp only [...]`) with the same core lemma list
(`Matrix.det_succ_row_zero, Fin.sum_univ_five, Fin.sum_univ_four, Fin.sum_univ_three,
Matrix.submatrix_apply, Fin.succAbove`) — letting simp's default lemma set additionally handle the
Fin-numeral/`cons_val` normalization that the restricted set was missing — followed by `ring` (for the
symbolic formula) or `norm_num` (for concrete numeric instances). Verified on isolated test files before
touching the real brick (three throwaway `TestNxN.lean` probes on Olympus, deleted after use).

**Lesson (important, general):** `simp only [L1, L2, ...]` and `simp [L1, L2, ...]` are NOT
interchangeable "the same set plus maybe a few extras" — for `Matrix`/`Fin` cofactor-expansion goals
specifically, the *default* simp set carries essential `Fin`-numeral and `Matrix.cons_val`-family
normalization lemmas that aren't in any short hand-picked list. When a hand-curated `simp only` stalls on
a goal full of unresolved `if`/`Fin.succAbove`/numeral-indexed `cons_val` terms, try widening to plain
`simp` with the same custom lemmas ADDED (not substituted) before concluding the approach doesn't scale —
this fixed a genuine wall at `n=5` that looked, at first, like it might require abandoning the direct
`Matrix.det` literal-computation approach entirely.

## §2086 (2026-09-06 02:23 CDT) — WeilSingleFlipGeneralFormula.lean — the general Kn single-flip formula

**Result:** answers the question named at the end of the §2085 consolidation. Computed the single-
edge-flip Gram determinant via sympy for `n=3,4,5,6,7` (extending the already-Lean-verified `n=3,4,5`

exactly), `n=6` and `n=7` are fresh checks against the direct sympy matrix computation, both matching

## §2087 (2026-09-06 02:27 CDT) — WeilSingleFlipThresholdMonotone.lean — the monotone-decrease mechanism, proven for all n

**Result:** upgrades the empirically-observed monotone-decreasing threshold trend (§2081-§2086:
`0.5, 0.447, 0.4215, 0.4058, 0.3951, ...`) from a pattern across five data points into a genuine theorem
holding for EVERY `n` at once — via pure real-number algebra, no Matrix machinery, no induction over
`Fin n` needed at all.

**Two clean algebraic facts carry the whole argument:**
1. `consecutive_quadratic_difference`: for the quadratic family `q_n(x) = (3n-7)x² - (n-4)x - 1`
   identified in §2086, consecutive levels differ by EXACTLY `x(3x-1)` — completely independent of `n`.
   A one-line `ring` identity.
2. `universal_floor_value`: `q_n(1/3) = -4/9` for EVERY `n` — a beautifully clean universal constant
   (also `ring`). Combined with `quadratic_positive_at_one` (`q_n(1) ≥ 2 > 0` for `n≥3`), this traps the
   actual positive root of every level's quadratic strictly inside `(1/3, 1)`.

**The main theorem (`threshold_strictly_decreases`):** if `x` is level `n`'s threshold (`q_n(x)=0`) and
`x > 1/3` (always true, by the floor fact), then `q_{n+1}(x) = q_n(x) + x(3x-1) = x(3x-1) > 0` (since
both `x>0` and `3x-1>0` when `x>1/3`). Since `q_{n+1}` is negative near `0` and this shows it's ALREADY
positive at `x` (level `n`'s own threshold), level `(n+1)`'s actual threshold must be strictly smaller
than `x`. This is the complete, general mechanism — proven once, valid at every step, no need to verify
five separate numeric instances ever again.

**Why this matters:** turns §2086's Report-tier empirical formula into something closer to Handle-tier —
not the full closed-form-for-all-n claim (that would still need the general determinant formula proven
by induction, not yet attempted), but the SPECIFIC claim that mattered most for the whole sub-thread
(density/frustration monotonically tightens realizability) is now a genuine proven theorem, not just five
confirmed data points. Also pins down `1/3` as the sequence's limiting floor — approached from above,
never reached — connecting back to §2082's K4 "all-four-triangles-frustrated" threshold (`x=1/3` exactly)
via a completely independent route (pure single-edge density in the `n→∞` limit, vs. multi-triangle
frustration at fixed `n=4`). Two unrelated mechanisms converging on the same constant is a genuinely
interesting structural coincidence worth flagging for future investigation.

Compiled on Olympus (`~/rhforge/forge/WeilSingleFlipThresholdMonotone.lean`), `.olean` built. All 4
theorems: `#print axioms` → `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`. EXIT0, zero sorry, first-attempt
clean (both `nlinarith` calls closed immediately given the exact hint terms).

**Lesson:** when a discovered pattern involves algebraic objects with more structure than "here are five
numbers" (in this case, a whole PARAMETRIZED FAMILY of quadratics), look for a relation between
CONSECUTIVE members of the family before assuming a full closed-form induction is the only path to
rigor — the recursion `q_{n+1}-q_n = x(3x-1)` was much cheaper to find and prove than a general
determinant-lemma induction would have been, and it proved the part of the claim (monotonicity) that
mattered most for this arc's actual question.

numerical coincidence? Found something more precise than either answer: sympy-testing the two-disjoint-
edges pattern extended to `n=4..9` shows `x=1/3` is an EXACT root (`(3x-1)` an exact algebraic factor of
the determinant) at EVERY `n` tested — not an asymptotic limit like §2087's single-flip family, a genuine
exact zero at every finite size.

**The mechanism (found by hand before writing Lean):** writing the sign matrix as `S` (with `S_ii=1`,
off-diagonal `±1` per the two-disjoint-edge pattern) and testing candidate eigenvectors, `v=(1,1,-1,-1,
0,...,0)` satisfies `S·v = -2·v` EXACTLY, for any `n≥4`. Why this holds independent of `n`: any vertex
beyond the core four connects with sign `+1` to ALL of the first four (neither flipped edge touches it),
and `v` restricted to the core four sums to `1+1-1-1=0` — so every "extra" row of `S·v` collapses to
`(+1)·0 = 0` automatically, regardless of how many extra vertices exist. This fixed eigenvalue `-2` forces
`(1-x)+x(-2) = 1-3x = 0`, i.e. `x=1/3`, to be an exact root of `det((1-x)I+xS)` at every `n`.

**So: are the two `1/3`s the same phenomenon?** No — genuinely different mechanisms (§2087's is a
large-`n` asymptotic limit of the single-edge family; this is an exact, finite-`n`, algebraic root of the
two-disjoint-edge family) that happen to land on the same constant. Both are now independently, honestly
explained rather than left as an unresolved coincidence.

instance, K5's two-disjoint-edges determinant evaluated exactly at `x=1/3`, confirmed `=0` via direct
`Matrix.det` computation (extending §2082's K4 case, where this fact was already implicit in the banked
`(3x-1)` factor but never evaluated as a standalone numeric check). `core_eigenvector_eigenvalue_neg_two`
— the abstract 4×4 mechanism itself, `S·v = -2v`, proven directly via `Matrix.mulVec`/`fin_cases`/
`norm_num`, isolating the actual algebraic reason from the surrounding `n`-dependent scaffolding.

**Lesson:** when investigating "is this a coincidence," look for the underlying LINEAR-ALGEBRA mechanism
(an eigenvector/eigenvalue) rather than just computing more numeric instances — it not only answers the

checking can never distinguish.
