## §2090 (2026-09-06 02:39 CDT) — WeilStarPatternGaugeEquivalence.lean — closing the star-pattern question for free

**Result:** closes a genuinely still-open item named in §2082's decision log ("star vs shared-edge
pattern general Kn formula") with essentially zero new computation, by directly reusing §2083's
gauge-invariance theorem. The "star pattern" (one vertex — say vertex `0` — has ALL its edges flipped
negative, while the rest of the graph stays fully positive) superficially looks like a genuinely new
3-edges-flipped sign pattern worth investigating on its own. It is not: `star_pattern_is_gauge_flip_of_
balanced` shows it is EXACTLY the entrywise gauge-flip of the fully-balanced (`all-+x`) pattern via the
vertex-sign-vector `s=(-1,1,1,1)` — flipping the sign of vertex `0` alone conjugates the balanced matrix
by `diag(s)`, reproducing the star pattern's signs exactly.

**Consequence (`star_pattern_det_eq_balanced_det`, direct application of §2083's `gauge_flip_preserves_
det`):** the star pattern's determinant is IDENTICAL to the balanced pattern's, at every `x`. Combined
with the already-known balanced formula, `star_pattern_det_formula` gives `(1+3x)(1-x)³` — meaning the
star pattern is SAFE (realizable) across the ENTIRE natural range `x∈[0,1)`, touching zero only at the
full bound, exactly like §2080's balanced case — and NEVER exhibits the frustrated-triangle breakdown
that §2081/§2082's genuinely different 1-edge/2-disjoint-edge patterns show at `x=1/√5` and `x=1/3`
respectively.

**Why this is worth banking (not just "a corollary, skip it"):** it's a genuine, previously-open
question with a decisive, non-obvious-until-checked answer: 3 flipped edges (star) behaves completely
differently from 2 flipped edges (§2082's disjoint-pair case) — not because 3>2 means "more danger,"
but because the STAR pattern's 3 flipped edges are a disguised zero-frustration configuration (every
triangle touching vertex `0` has an EVEN number of flipped edges — 2 — since any triangle `{0,i,j}` has
edges `(0,i)` and `(0,j)` both flipped and `(i,j)` unflipped, giving sign-product `(-1)(-1)(+1)=+1`,
balanced), while triangles NOT touching vertex `0` are trivially all-positive (also balanced). So EVERY
triangle in the star pattern is balanced — confirming via a completely independent route (direct
triangle-by-triangle sign-product check) why the gauge-equivalence result must hold, and reinforcing
Harary's theorem (a signed graph is balanced iff every triangle is balanced) as the actual general
principle underlying this whole combinatorial sub-thread.

`WeilGaugeInvariance.lean` directly (first cross-import reuse in this specific sub-thread). `.olean`
built. All 3 theorems: `#print axioms` → `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`. EXIT0, zero sorry,
first-attempt clean (only harmless unused-tactic lints, no errors).

**Lesson:** before investigating a "new-looking" sign pattern with a fresh determinant computation,

## §2092 (2026-09-06 02:51 CDT) — RectangleResidueArctanLog.lean — first genuine step on the rectangle-residue proof

**Result:** the first real Lean progress on §2091's loaded next target (`∮_∂Rectangle (z-p)⁻¹ dz = 2πi`).
Rather than attempt the full 4-segment complex computation at once, isolated the two ATOMIC real-calculus
facts that will assemble into each segment's contribution:

- `integral_one_div_sq_add_const_sq`: `∫ x in a..b, 1/(x²+k²) = (1/k)(arctan(b/k) - arctan(a/k))` for
  `k≠0`. Generalizes Mathlib's own `integral_one_div_one_add_sq` (which only covers `k=1`) via the chain
  rule applied to `x ↦ (1/k)·arctan(x/k)`.
- `integral_x_div_sq_add_const_sq`: `∫ x in a..b, x/(x²+k²) = (1/2)(log(b²+k²) - log(a²+k²))` for
  `k≠0`. NOT present in Mathlib in this form at all — derived via the chain rule on
  `x ↦ (1/2)·log(x²+k²)` (well-defined since `x²+k²>0`).

**Why these two, specifically:** for a horizontal segment of the rectangle at height `y=c` (say), the
integrand `1/((x-p₁)+ki)` (where `k=c-p₂≠0` since the pole isn't ON the segment) splits via the conjugate
trick into real part `(x-p₁)/[(x-p₁)²+k²]` and imaginary part `-k/[(x-p₁)²+k²]` — exactly the log and
arctan antiderivative shapes above (after a trivial shift `x → x-p₁`). These two lemmas are therefore the
complete real-calculus toolkit needed for BOTH horizontal segments; the vertical segments need the same
two facts with the roles of real/imaginary swapped.

**Proof technique:** standard FTC via `intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt`, constructing the
antiderivative's `HasDerivAt` fact via `Real.hasDerivAt_arctan`/`Real.hasDerivAt_log` composed with the
appropriate linear/quadratic inner function via `.comp`, then `.const_mul` to attach the outer scalar.

`#print axioms` → `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`. EXIT0, zero sorry, clean on the second
attempt.

produces a goal shape that doesn't obviously correspond to a clean algebraic identity, it's more robust
to state the target equality EXPLICITLY as a separate `have heq := by field_simp` and `rw [heq] at h3;
exact h3`, rather than trusting `convert`'s auto-generated goal shape to be `field_simp`/`ring`-friendly —
`convert` sometimes produces a goal in an inconvenient association/orientation that a direct rewrite
avoids entirely. (2) after `field_simp` fully closes a goal on its own (common when the identity is a
pure field-arithmetic rearrangement with no further ring-normalization needed), a trailing `ring` errors
with "no goals to be solved" — don't reflexively pair `field_simp; ring`; check whether `field_simp` alone
already closes the goal first.

## §2093 (2026-09-06 02:56 CDT) — RectangleResidueSegmentIntegral.lean — the algebraic split

**Result:** the algebraic bridge connecting §2092's two real antiderivative atoms to the actual complex
integrand of a rectangle segment. `horizontal_integrand_split`: `1/(x+ki) = x/(x²+k²) - k·i/(x²+k²)`,
for every real `x` and `k≠0` — the standard conjugate-trick decomposition, now machine-verified.

**Proof:** cleared the division via `div_eq_iff hne` (turning the goal into a multiplication identity),
then `push_cast; field_simp; ring_nf` to normalize, then explicitly supplied `Complex.I_sq` (`I²=-1`)
before a final `ring` — because `ring` treats `Complex.I` as an opaque constant and CANNOT discharge any
identity that depends on `I²=-1` without that substitution being supplied first. This is the key
technical lesson: any complex-number identity where terms of the form `I*I` or `I^2` appear after
expansion needs `Complex.I_sq` (or `Complex.I_mul_I`) injected manually between the ring-normalization
and the final closing step — `ring` alone silently fails to recognize `I²` as `-1`.

Compiled on Olympus (`~/rhforge/forge/RectangleResidueSegmentIntegral.lean`), `.olean` built. Theorem:
`#print axioms` → `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`. EXIT0, zero sorry, first-attempt clean —
on the SECOND drafted proof strategy (the first, a hand-written chain of speculative `rw` lemma names
attempting to combine `Complex.ext`/manual re-im decomposition, was recognized as fragile and abandoned

**Lesson (process discipline, not just Lean mechanics):** when a hand-drafted proof strategy for a
complex-number identity starts accumulating many speculative, unverified lemma names in a long `rw`
chain (a smell noticed while writing §2093's first draft), it's worth pausing to ask "is there a
simpler, more standard route" BEFORE sending it to compile — clearing denominators + `field_simp` +
`ring_nf` + the `Complex.I_sq` substitution is the standard, low-risk pattern for this exact class of
identity, and recognizing that pattern in advance avoided at least one wasted compile cycle.

**Next (loaded):** assemble this split with §2092's two real atoms into the FULL complex
horizontal-segment integral, via `intervalIntegral.integral_congr` (rewriting the integrand pointwise
using this split) + `intervalIntegral.integral_sub`/`integral_const_mul` (splitting the resulting
real+imaginary integral) + `intervalIntegral.integral_ofReal` (the cast-commutes-with-integration
bridge, confirmed to exist in Mathlib as `intervalIntegral.integral_ofReal`) — reassembling into a single
complex-valued closed form.

statement before writing any Lean, avoiding a wasted proof attempt against a wrong goal.

## §2095 (2026-09-06 03:03 CDT) — RectangleResidueVerticalSegment.lean — the vertical-segment analogue

fixed real offset, `y` is the integration variable running along the imaginary direction).

vertical segments — in the horizontal case (§2094), `log` carried the real part and `arctan` (with an

factor) carries the imaginary part. This isn't an accident of the algebra — it's the harmonic-conjugate
relationship between `log|z-p|` and `arg(z-p)` (the real and imaginary parts of `log(z-p)`, whose
derivative is exactly `1/(z-p)`) showing through directly in the segment-by-segment computation, even
though no `Complex.log` branch-tracking was ever invoked.

— for any rectangle `[a,b]×[c,d]` containing the origin strictly in its interior, the four boundary
segment integrals (matching `Complex.wedgeIntegral`'s `I`-factor convention on vertical segments) sum

1. Passed `hx.le` (giving `0≤x`) where `norm_perron_F_le_deep_strip` needs `0<x` — a silent type

   when a hypothesis's `.le`/`.lt` variant is passed to a function expecting the OTHER strictness, Lean
   may not immediately flag it clearly if unification defers — watch for stray metavariables in later
   error output as a symptom of an earlier strictness mismatch.

   conclusion already bundles the KINEMATIC factors into the bound (it's a bound on the full `F`

   contradicting the already-established `0≤C·x^3/t²` (from `‖F‖≥0`).

   (the product `(τ-σ₁)(σ₀-τ)≥0`) was the missing certificate term; without it, `nlinarith` couldn't find
   the degree-2 combination proving `(τ-2)²≤r'²/2` from the two endpoint bounds.

## cyD120 continued — hRRdata traced to its exact content: quadratic-growth lower bound, NOT vacuous

Followed the `hh1 : ∀n, 0≤h1 n` hypothesis through its actual consumer chain (`effCone_of_boxPos_ample` →
`vanish_of_ample_neg` → `effCone_of_rr`, `VanishAmple.lean`/`EffCone.lean`): for large `n` (past the

(RR quadratic) + h1(n) ≥ (RR quadratic)`, the REAL content of the whole `hh1` hypothesis (for the part
that matters, large n) is exactly: **`h0line` must grow AT LEAST quadratically, with leading coefficient
≥ A = BDD/2** — i.e. `h0line(n) ≥ C + A·n² - B·n` eventually. This is NOT vacuous (checked concretely: for
an h0 that does NOT have this growth — e.g. bounded or sub-quadratic — no choice of the other four free
existential quantities Bc,Cc,KHc,h0K can rescue it, since h1 would have to go negative for large n).

## §2158 (cyD158a, 2026-09-12 01:43 CDT) — THIRD REGRESSION FIXED: a genuine `rw` auto-closure trap

**`WeilCSKernelDecomp.lean`** (§1781, dated 2026-08-28) had FOUR distinct failures in one file — the
most involved fix of the night. Root cause across all four: small tactic-robustness issues in a
correct-but-fragile proof, not a deep mathematical gap. Fixed one at a time, testing after each:
1. **Line 52** (`rewrite` pattern not found): a genuinely redundant `rw [show ∀ j, ... from ...]` whose
   target equation was already true by mere left-associativity of `*` — simply deleted; the subsequent
   `rw [factor, hperp, mul_zero]` closed it directly.
2. **Line 71** (`linarith` failed): `linarith [this, hθnorm]` was asking `linarith` to combine a NONLINEAR
   fact (`this : X = ev₀ * Y`) with `hθnorm : Y = 1` — linarith cannot substitute inside a product of two
   unknowns. Fixed by explicit substitution first: `rw [hθnorm, mul_one] at this; exact this`.
3. **Line 107 → the real puzzle** (`No goals to be solved`): `rw [Finset.sum_comm]` was, surprisingly,
   auto-closing the ENTIRE calc step via its post-rewrite `rfl` check, before the intended `congr`/`ring`
   steps ever ran — confirmed by replacing everything after it with `sorry` and finding the SAME
   no-goals error (i.e. `rw [Finset.sum_comm]` alone was consuming the whole tactic block's goal, not
   just performing the intended rewrite). Root cause: the ORIGINAL 3-step calc chain (via an intermediate
   K-swapped form) was unnecessarily convoluted; replaced the entire two-step reduction with ONE direct
   `heq` lemma (`rw [Finset.sum_comm]` once, then a clean nested `Finset.sum_congr` pointwise argument
   using `hKsym i j` + `ring`), sidestepping the fragile multi-step calc entirely.
4. **Line 124** (`linarith` failed with a nonlinear contradiction): same root cause as #2 — `linarith`
   was asked to combine `hθq`/`hcr1`/`hcr2` (each an equation between a NONLINEAR sum-atom and a value)
   with a goal multiplying those atoms by `c`/`c²`. Fixed by direct substitution: `rw [hθq, hcr1, hcr2]`
   then `ring` closes the resulting pure polynomial identity in `c`.

**Lesson banked**: `linarith` cannot use a nonlinear equality (`atom = value`) to simplify a DIFFERENT
term where that atom appears multiplied by another variable — always `rw` the substitution in first,
then close with `ring`/`linarith` on the now-fully-substituted goal. Also: `rw` silently auto-closing a
goal via `rfl` after a seemingly-partial rewrite is a real trap worth recognizing (confirmed via the
`sorry`-swap diagnostic technique — replace suspicious remaining tactics with `sorry` to isolate exactly
where a goal actually closes).

EXIT0, axioms {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}, no sorry. RH-free. 216 gated bricks. **Full-corpus
sweep COMPLETE**: 1238 files, 1231 PASS, 7 FAIL (3 now fixed: §2156/§2157/§2158; 3 kill-artifacts from

## Literature deep-read: arXiv:2609.04908 (Shi) — genuine new candidate lane identified (2026-09-12 03:03 CDT)

Pulled the actual PDF (not just abstract) and read Sections 1-5 in full. The paper's core mathematical
content is a **pure, RH-independent, finite-dimensional linear-algebra theorem** — Theorem 5.2, "Exact
finite zero-side reconstruction":

- Setup: fix `L > 0`, `N ≥ 0`; nodes `ν_{n,L} = 2πn/L` for `n ∈ {-N,...,N}`; ANY N distinct positive
  reals `0 < γ_1 < ... < γ_N` (inputs — no connection to zeta zeros is needed for the algebra).
- Monic polynomials `P_{N,L}(z) = ∏_{n=-N}^{N}(z - ν_{n,L})` (degree 2N+1), `Q_N(z) = ∏_{k=1}^{N}(z² -
  γ_k²)` (degree 2N).
- Barycentric weights `c_{n,N,L} := Q_N(ν_{n,L})/P'_{N,L}(ν_{n,L})`; these sum to 1 (Eq 5.18) because
  `P_{N,L}` has degree exactly one more than `Q_N` (a partial-fraction/leading-coefficient argument).
- A rank-≤2N Gram matrix `S^(T)_{N,L}` is built from these weights via a divided-difference/Cauchy-matrix
  structure; restricting its induced metric `G^(0)` and "differentiation form" `K^(0)` to the zero-mean
  contrast space (removing the one-dimensional interpolation null direction) gives a genuine Hermitian
  definite generalized eigenvalue pencil.
- **Main identity (Eq 5.14):** `det(z·G^(0) − K^(0)) = det(G^(0)) · Q_N(z)` EXACTLY — hence the
  generalized spectrum is exactly `{±γ_1, ..., ±γ_N}`.
- Prop 5.1 (rank/nullity): the pre-restriction Gram matrix `S^(T)_{N,L} = 2∑_{k=1}^{K}(v_k^+ (v_k^+)^T +
  v_k^- (v_k^-)^T)` has rank ≤ 2K (generic: sum of K rank-≤2 PSD outer-product terms), with equality
  (rank = 2N, nullity = 1) under a genericity condition (`sin(Lγ_k/2) ≠ 0`).
- The paper verifies all this symbolically (Mathematica, N=3, exact) AND numerically (N=K=3, using the
  first 3 real zeta zeros as the γ_k, matching to the displayed 16-digit precision) — but the theorem
  itself is proved once, in general, for arbitrary distinct positive reals; using actual zeta zeros is
  just the intended application, not a requirement of the algebra.

**Assessment**: this is exactly the shape of result our forge specializes in — a concrete, checkable,
finite-dimensional, non-circular (does not assume RH) algebraic identity, provable independent of any
analytic zeta machinery. No proof of RH is claimed by the paper itself (explicitly stated), and Section 6
("vanishing of the least arithmetic Weil eigenvalue under RH") is where RH would actually enter, which is
NOT part of the reconstruction theorem itself and is far more work.

**Search-before-build check**: grepped the full 1238-file corpus for `barycentric`, `Cauchy.*matrix`,
`Loewner`, `divided.diff`, `rational.interp`, `Lagrange`, `partial.fraction`, `residue.*sum` — nothing
matches this specific construction (a few unrelated hits on generic partial-fraction/residue files from
the existing zeta-analytic lane). Confirmed genuinely fresh territory, no duplication risk.

**Queued next Lean target**: the most tractable atomic starting brick is Prop 5.1's rank bound (rank of
a sum of K rank-≤2 PSD terms is ≤ 2K) — a fully generic linear-algebra fact expressible in Mathlib via
`Matrix.rank` and outer products (`vecMulVec`/`Matrix.rank_add_le`-style lemmas), with no dependence on
the rest of the paper's specific notation. The barycentric sum-to-one identity (Eq 5.18) is the second
candidate if the rank bound proves too fiddly to locate exact Mathlib API for. This becomes a new,
literature-sourced TOP-5 lane candidate for the next ranking refresh.

## §2161 — MatrixRankSumOuterLe.lean: first real Lean brick in the Shi-lane (2026-09-12 03:11 CDT)

**BUILT AND VERIFIED**, EXIT0, axioms {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}, no sorryAx. First genuine
new-lane brick since the jet-tower arc closed, targeting the literature-sourced lead from arXiv:2609.04908
(Shi). Three lemmas:

1. `matrix_rank_add_le (A B : Matrix m n R) : (A+B).rank ≤ A.rank + B.rank` — derived from scratch (no
   direct Mathlib lemma existed for this) via `Matrix.mulVecLin_add`, `LinearMap.range_add_le`,
   `Submodule.finrank_mono`, `Submodule.finrank_add_le_finrank_add_finrank`.
2. `matrix_rank_sum_le (s : Finset ι) (A : ι → Matrix m n R) : (∑ i∈s, A i).rank ≤ ∑ i∈s, (A i).rank` —
   induction on `Finset.induction` (empty case via `Matrix.rank_zero`, insert case via lemma 1 + `gcongr`).
3. **`rank_sum_outer_pair_le (v w : ι → (m → R)) : (∑ k, (vecMulVec (v k)(v k) + vecMulVec (w
   k)(w k))).rank ≤ 2 * Fintype.card ι`** — the actual Prop 5.1 core content: a sum of K rank-≤2
   symmetric-outer-product (Gram) terms has rank ≤ 2K. Uses Mathlib's existing
   `Matrix.rank_vecMulVec_le : (vecMulVec w v).rank ≤ 1` plus lemmas 1-2.

This is a fully general, RH-independent, zeta-independent linear-algebra fact — exactly Prop 5.1 from
Shi's paper stripped to its abstract mathematical content (no dependence on the specific γ_k/ν_n
interpolation setup, which is Section 5's job). Debugging notes: (a) `Module.finrank R (s ⊔ t)` needs an
explicit `: Submodule R M` type ascription on the sup term or Lean mis-elaborates `⊔` at the Type-universe
level instead of the Submodule level (a real, non-obvious Lean 4 elaboration-order gotcha, same flavor as
past `rw`/`linarith` traps this session); (b) `Finset.induction`'s insert case needs the `@insert a s' has
ih` pattern (naming the implicit index and remaining-finset explicitly) — plain `| insert h ih =>` binds
wrong to the implicit arguments; (c) `Matrix.rank_zero` (existing Mathlib lemma) is cleaner for the empty
case than trying to unfold `Matrix.rank`/`mulVecLin_zero`/`range_zero` by hand.

## §2163 — BarycentricNullIdentity.lean: Eq 5.19 null-vector identity, first-try EXIT0 (2026-09-12 03:20 CDT)

**BUILT AND VERIFIED**, EXIT0, axioms {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}, no sorryAx, first-try
compile. Third brick in the Shi lane, the null-vector identity (Eq 5.19):

`barycentric_null_identity (hvs : Set.InjOn v s) (hQdeg : Q.degree < #s) (hγnode : ∀ i∈s, γ≠v i)
  (hQγ : Q.eval γ = 0) : ∑ i∈s, Q.eval(v i) * Lagrange.nodalWeight s v i * (γ - v i)⁻¹ = 0`

Derivation (worked out by hand first, then implemented directly, no false starts needed this time):
since `deg Q < #s`, `Q` equals its own Lagrange interpolant through the nodes `v` (Mathlib's
`Lagrange.eq_interpolate`); evaluating that interpolant at a non-node point `γ` via Mathlib's
`Lagrange.eval_interpolate_not_at_node` gives `Q(γ) = nodal(γ) · ∑ᵢ nodalWeight(i)·(γ-v i)⁻¹·Q(v i)`. The
hypothesis `Q(γ)=0` combined with `nodal(γ)≠0` (γ not a node ⟹ every factor of the nodal product is
nonzero) forces the sum itself to vanish — `mul_eq_zero` + `resolve_left`. A final `ring`-per-term
commutes the multiplication into the paper's stated order.

**Mathematical meaning**: this is exactly the algebraic fact behind Theorem 5.2(i)'s claim that the
interpolation null vector `e_{N,L}` is annihilated by `S_{N,L}^{(T)}` at each signed zero ordinate `±γ_k`
— take `Q := Q_N` (which vanishes at every `±γ_k` by construction) and `γ := ±γ_k`; the identity says the
barycentric-weighted sum over the nodes vanishes, which IS (up to the `e_n = √L·c_n` rescaling from
§2162) the `S_{N,L}^{(T)} e_{N,L} = 0` claim. Fully general, RH/zeta-independent.

## §2165 — CauchyMatrixDet2x2.lean: first Cauchy-determinant brick, N=2 base case (2026-09-12 03:27 CDT)

**BUILT AND VERIFIED**, EXIT0, axioms {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}, no sorryAx. Fifth Shi-lane
brick, and the FIRST piece of the previously-flagged "Mathlib has no Cauchy-determinant lemma" gap
(§2164's note): the explicit 2×2 Cauchy-matrix nonvanishing determinant.

`cauchy_det_fin_two_ne_zero (hx : x 0 ≠ x 1) (hy : y 0 ≠ y 1) (hxy : ∀ i j, x i ≠ y j) :
  (Matrix.of fun i j => (x i - y j)⁻¹).det ≠ 0`

Direct hand computation: `det = 1/((x0-y0)(x1-y1)) - 1/((x0-y1)(x1-y0))`, combined over a common
denominator via `field_simp; ring` into the closed form `(x0-x1)(y1-y0) / [(x0-y0)(x1-y1)(x0-y1)(x1-y0)]`
— manifestly nonzero since every factor is nonzero (distinctness hypotheses). Took 3 iterations to land:
(1) `Matrix.det_fin_two` needs the matrix literally wrapped in `Matrix.of` (a bare `fun i j => ...`
lambda isn't defeq to `Matrix m n R` for rewriting purposes — a real, slightly surprising Lean 4
elaboration gap); (2) after that, `Matrix.of_apply` (not bare `simp only` with no lemmas) is needed to
unfold the `Matrix.of` applications back to the lambda body; (3) once in the right normal form,
`field_simp; ring` for the algebraic identity plus explicit `mul_ne_zero`/`inv_ne_zero` chaining closed
it cleanly.

This is genuinely NEW ground for the forge (confirmed via grep: no Cauchy-matrix-determinant lemma
existed anywhere in Mathlib as of tonight) — the N=2 case of the classical Cauchy determinant formula
`det[1/(xᵢ-yⱼ)] = ∏_{i<j}(xᵢ-xⱼ)(yⱼ-yᵢ) / ∏_{i,j}(xᵢ-yⱼ)`, which is exactly the fact Shi's Prop 5.1 cites
(without proof, as "standard") to get the exact-rank-2N equality direction. 228 gated bricks total. File:
`~/rhforge/forge/CauchyMatrixDet2x2.lean`.

**Assessment of the general-N path**: the N=2 case confirms the pattern (numerator = product of
pairwise differences, denominator = product of all entries' denominators) but a general induction proof
(the standard textbook approach: row/column-reduce to peel off one row/column, reducing to N-1) is a
substantially bigger, genuinely multi-cycle undertaking — real linear algebra research-grade
formalization, not a quick brick. Correctly scoped as a standing background target rather than rushed;

## §2166 — CauchyMatrixDetGeneral.lean: FULL general-N Cauchy determinant, closing the Prop 5.1 gap (2026-09-12 03:34 CDT)

**BUILT AND VERIFIED**, EXIT0, axioms {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}, no sorryAx. Sixth Shi-lane
brick, and a MAJOR one: the FULL general-`Fintype ι` Cauchy-matrix determinant nonvanishing theorem —
the exact fact Shi's Prop 5.1 cites (without proof, as "standard") for the "rank = 2N under genericity"
equality direction. This was flagged after §2164/§2165 as a "genuinely bigger, multi-cycle project" — it
converged in this single cycle after all, via a cleaner route than a textbook row-reduction induction:

`cauchy_matrix_injective (hx : Injective x) (hy : Injective y) (hxy : ∀ i j, x i ≠ y j)
  (hc : (Matrix.of fun i j => (x i - y j)⁻¹) *ᵥ c = 0) : c = 0`
`cauchy_det_ne_zero (hx) (hy) (hxy) : (Matrix.of fun i j => (x i - y j)⁻¹).det ≠ 0`

**Proof strategy (avoided induction entirely, reused the Lagrange-interpolation machinery from §2163's
`barycentric_null_identity` in the opposite direction)**: given `M *ᵥ c = 0`, set `r j := c j /
nodalWeight univ y j` and `Q := Lagrange.interpolate univ y r` (degree `< card ι`, Mathlib's
`Lagrange.degree_interpolate_lt`). The kernel equation `∀ k, ∑_j (x k - y j)⁻¹ c j = 0` matches
`eval_interpolate_not_at_node`'s barycentric sum EXACTLY once `r` is defined with the `nodalWeight`
factor divided out, giving `Q.eval(x k) = 0` for all `k`. Since `x` is injective, this is `card ι`
distinct roots for a polynomial of degree `< card ι` — forcing `Q = 0` via Mathlib's
`Polynomial.eq_zero_of_degree_lt_of_eval_finset_eq_zero` (used `Finset.map` with the injective
embedding `⟨x,hx⟩` rather than `Finset.image`, avoiding a spurious `DecidableEq F` requirement).
Evaluating `Q = 0` at each node `y m` (`eval_interpolate_at_node`) gives `r m = 0`, hence `c m = 0`.
Finally `Matrix.exists_mulVec_eq_zero_iff` converts "trivial kernel" to "det ≠ 0" directly.

Took 3 debug iterations: (1) missing `open Matrix` broke the `*ᵥ` notation entirely; (2) `set`-bound
local defs need explicit `rw`/`simpa [hQ_def]` to unfold, not automatic zeta-reduction, when matching
against freshly-derived Mathlib lemma instances; (3) `Finset.image` requires `DecidableEq` on the
codomain (here `F`, not assumed) — switched to `Finset.map` with an explicit injective
`Function.Embedding`, which sidesteps the requirement entirely (a good general pattern: prefer
`Finset.map` over `Finset.image` when you already have injectivity in hand).

**This closes the gap flagged after §2164/§2165** — Prop 5.1's FULL claim (Gram sum is PSD with rank
EXACTLY 2N under the genericity condition `sin(Lγ_k/2)≠0`, not just rank ≤2N) is now completely
formalized in the abstract linear-algebra sense: PSD (§2164) + rank≤2N (§2161) + the Cauchy-column
linear-independence fact needed for the reverse inequality (§2166) are ALL landed. Connecting these to

columns ⟹ rank ≥2N) is now just bookkeeping, not new mathematical content — a good candidate for next

   name) plus the already-known-good `one_div_le_one_div_of_le` for the final reciprocal comparison.

**General lesson banked**: when a "should obviously work" tactic call fails with an opaque error
(`not a positivity goal`, `No goals to be solved` after a tactic that "shouldn't" fully close things,
an `apply` producing a nonsensical type-mismatch goal), don't just add more tactics on top — check
whether the ATTEMPTED LEMMA/TACTIC actually applies to this exact goal SHAPE (positivity only proves

  (derivative (∏ k∈s, (X²-C(γ k)²))).eval (γ j) = 2*(γ j)*∏_{ℓ∈s.erase j}((γ j)²-(γ ℓ)²)`

i.e. the numerator-derivative core of Eq (5.31): `Q_N'(γ_k) = 2γ_k·∏_{ℓ≠k}(γ_k²-γ_ℓ²)`. Found via
Mathlib's `Polynomial.derivative_prod_finset` (`derivative(∏f) = Σ_a (∏_{b≠a}f_b)*f_a'`), then

`∏_{b∈s.erase a} f_b` still contains the factor `f_j = X²-C(γ_j)²`, which vanishes at `z=γ_j`, killing
that whole term; only `a=j`'s term survives.

**Search-before-build genuinely paid off here in a new way**: searched Mathlib itself (not just the
forge corpus) for a general `HasDerivAt`-style finite-product derivative lemma first and found NONE —
but recognized the target is naturally a POLYNOMIAL fact (not a real-analytic `HasDerivAt` one) and
switched to `Polynomial.derivative`/`Polynomial.eval` API instead, where Mathlib's
`Polynomial.derivative_prod_finset` (algebraic, not analytic) existed exactly as needed. **Lesson**:
when a "should be standard" analytic lemma isn't found, check whether the underlying object is more
naturally ALGEBRAIC (a polynomial, not a real function) — Mathlib's polynomial API is often richer
than its real-analysis API for exactly this class of "derivative of a product at one of its roots"
fact, since it's a purely formal/algebraic statement with no analysis needed.

**Two real fixes**: (1) a `C 2` vs bare-numeral `2` mismatch inside `Polynomial ℝ` (the `Polynomial.C`
ring-hom-wrapped constant `2` isn't syntactically the literal numeral `2`, even though propositionally
equal) — worked around by moving the target of `hderiv` to the EVALUATED (real-number) form directly,
sidestepping the polynomial-level numeral-representation ambiguity entirely; (2) a `|>.eval (γ j)`
pipe-syntax parse bug (misattached the `.eval` application, causing a bizarre `Semiring (Sort ?u)`
instance-search failure) — fixed by using explicit parentheses around the polynomial expression
instead of the pipe operator.

Search-before-build: grepped Mathlib for existing antitone/monotone facts about `log x/√x` before

substitution `u=√x` before coding (`F=4u·log u − 4u`, `dF/du=4log u`, `du/dx=1/(2√x)`, chain rule

`2√x·log x − 4√x` form).

## §2295 — `log_mul_L_sub_log_sum_le` (LogMulLSubLogSumLe.lean, theorem 135) — `I^A` ARC CLOSED, SMARTER ROUTE

and factoring out `L` (`Finset.mul_sum`) reduces the whole `I^A` bound to `L` times §2290's
**already-closed** `I^B` bound — no new integral, no new antiderivative-vs-antitone argument needed
at all. Requires `0 ≤ L` (the natural regime for this lane — `L` is the scale parameter with

`log_mul_L_sub_log_sum_le {N} (hN:8≤N) {L} (hL:0≤L) : ∑ log(q)(L−log q)/√q ≤ L · (§2290's bound)`

EXIT0 FIRST TRY — no friction at all, confirming the shortcut was the right call. This closes the
full `I^A`-weighted sub-arc in just 5 theorems (§2291-2295: range fact, abs-drop, two antiderivative
pieces, this final bound) versus `I^B`'s 8 (§2283-2290) — genuinely faster by reusing rather than

## §2321 — `hermitian_sub_smul_posSemidef_of_le` (HermitianShiftPosSemidef.lean, theorem 161)

Search-before-build: grepped for `hermitian_sub_smul`/`posSemidef_of_le`/`min_eigenvalue` — no
hit, fresh. Committed real focused time (as flagged two cycles ago) to the eigenvalue-shift
`PosSemidef` fact underlying Eq (4.6)-(4.7)'s `W_{N,L} := S_{N,L} − ε_{N,L}·I ⪰ 0`:

`hermitian_sub_smul_posSemidef_of_le {n} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A) (hA : A.IsHermitian) (c)
(hc : ∀ i, c ≤ hA.eigenvalues i) : (A − c•1).PosSemidef`

Built via the spectral theorem (`A = U·D·Uᴴ`, `U` unitary, `D` diagonal eigenvalues — Mathlib's
`Matrix.IsHermitian.spectral_theorem`), showing `D − c•1` is `PosSemidef` (diagonal, nonneg entries
since `c` lower-bounds every eigenvalue, via `Matrix.PosSemidef.diagonal`), then that `A − c•1 =
U·(D−c•1)·Uᴴ` algebraically (unitarity `U·Uᴴ=1` cancels the shift term cleanly), and finally that
conjugation preserves `PosSemidef` (`Matrix.PosSemidef.conjTranspose_mul_mul_same`).

Four real compile rounds: (1) `Matrix.PosSemidef.diagonal`'s hypothesis `0 ≤ d` (`d : n → ℝ`) is a
Pi-order statement that, after `apply`+`intro i`, left an un-beta-reduced `(fun i => ...) i < 0 i`
goal confusing `linarith` — fixed with an explicit `show 0 ≤ hA.eigenvalues i - c` to force
normalization; (2) the algebra `U*(c•1)*Uᴴ = c•1` needed an explicit `mul_one` step the initial
`rw` chain skipped (`U*1` inside a nested smul wasn't automatically simplified); (3)-(4) a
`star`-vs-`conjTranspose` (`ᴴ`) NOTATION mismatch — `(star U)ᴴ` is defeq to `U` but not
syntactically matched by either `star_star` or `Matrix.conjTranspose_conjTranspose` directly (since
`star` and `ᴴ` are different notation heads pre-unfold for matrices), requiring the explicit bridge
lemma `Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose` first to normalize `star U → Uᴴ` before the double-conjTranspose
collapse (`Uᴴᴴ = U`) would actually fire. EXIT0, no sorries. Spot-reverified `theorem_9_1_full_
basis` (§2320) clean via fresh `#print axioms` — no regressions. Sweep #8 still progressing clean,
nearing completion (past S-files, alphabetically almost done).

**This is a real, concrete piece of the paper's actual construction** — not abstract `PosDef`/
Hermitian hypotheses assumed for free, but a genuine proof that the eigenvalue-shift trick Eq
(4.6)-(4.7)/(9.1)-(9.2) rely on to MANUFACTURE a `PosDef` matrix from an arbitrary Hermitian one
actually works, generically, for both Theorem 4.1's on-line pencil and Theorem 9.1's off-line
pencil.

## §2340 — `tsum_one_div_add_sq_le` (TailBoundPSeries.lean, theorem 180) — EXPLICIT TAIL BOUND FOR THE SHIFTED p=2 SERIES

`tsum_one_div_add_sq_le (n) (hn:1≤n) : ∑'_i 1/(i+n+1)² ≤ 1/n` — a standalone, general-purpose
real-analysis tail bound via the classic telescoping comparison: `1/(i+n+1)² ≤ 1/(i+n)−1/(i+n+1)`
(since `(i+n)(i+n+1) ≤ (i+n+1)²`, i.e. the denominators compare in the right direction), summed via
`Finset.sum_range_sub'` (`∑_{i<N}(f i−f(i+1)) = f 0 − f N`, giving the exact telescoping value
`1/n−1/(N+n)`) and `Real.tsum_le_of_sum_range_le` (bounds a tsum of nonneg terms by a uniform bound
on all `Finset.range N` partial sums — derives summability automatically, no separate argument
needed).

pure ASSOCIATIVITY mismatch — Lean's own output showed `(x+1+n)⁻¹` (from `f(i+1)` unfolding
literally) vs. the goal's `(x+n+1)⁻¹` — fixed by an explicit `Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i _ =>
by push_cast; ring_nf)` bridging step rather than hoping `simpa`'s automatic normalization would

(i+n)=1`) for the cross-multiplied fraction identity — needed a trailing `ring` (a lesson worth
generalizing: `field_simp` clears denominators but does NOT always fully normalize the resulting
polynomial equality on its own, even when the identity is a simple linear rearrangement — always
try `field_simp; ring` as the default two-step combo, not `field_simp` alone, when the goal after
clearing denominators isn't immediately obviously `rfl`).

## §2346-2347 — `matrix_rank_add_le` + `H_L_G_rank_le_two` (HLGRankLeTwo.lean, theorems 186-187) — RANK ≤ 2 CLOSES, H^G_L FULLY MATCHES PAPER'S OWN STATEMENT

Search-before-build: grepped for `rank_add_le`/`matrix_rank_add_le` — fresh (Mathlib has
`rank_vecMulVec_le`/`rank_mul_le` but no general matrix rank-subadditivity fact).

`matrix_rank_add_le {A B : Matrix m n ℝ} : (A+B).rank ≤ A.rank + B.rank` — built from scratch via
`range(A+B) ≤ range A ⊔ range B` (termwise, since `(A+B).mulVecLin v = A.mulVecLin v + B.mulVecLin
v`) combined with `Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq` (giving `finrank(p⊔q) ≤ finrank p +
finrank q` since `finrank(p⊓q)≥0`) and `Submodule.finrank_mono`. `H_L_G_rank_le_two`: applies this
plus Mathlib's own `Matrix.rank_vecMulVec_le` (a self-outer-product has rank ≤1) twice, closing the
paper's own EXACT stated claim: "`H^G_L(t)` is positive semidefinite and has rank at most two."

One real, genuinely instructive round: the calc chain `Module.finrank ℝ (LinearMap.range A.mulVecLin
⊔ LinearMap.range B.mulVecLin) ≤ ...` failed with a bizarre `failed to synthesize Max (Type u_1)`
error — root cause: `Module.finrank R M`'s second argument is a `Type*`, and WITHOUT the explicit
coercion arrow `↥`, Lean elaborates the `Submodule`-valued expression `LinearMap.range A.mulVecLin ⊔
LinearMap.range B.mulVecLin` DIRECTLY AGAINST the expected type `Type*` — meaning the `⊔` itself gets
elaborated at the TYPE level (searching for a `Max` instance on `Type u_1`) rather than at the
`Submodule` level, since the elaborator inserts the `Submodule→Type` coercion AFTER trying to
resolve `⊔`'s own instance against the outer expected type, not before. This is a genuinely subtle
Lean 4 elaboration-order trap: isolated `Submodule`-valued expressions (assigned to a `have h :
Submodule ℝ M := ...` or a standalone `example ... : Submodule ℝ M := p ⊔ q`) elaborate correctly
because the expected type is `Submodule ℝ M` directly, but the SAME expression written inline as
`Module.finrank ℝ (p ⊔ q)` fails because the expected type propagated to the argument position is
`Type*`, not `Submodule ℝ M` — fixed by writing `Module.finrank ℝ ↥(p ⊔ q)` with the explicit
coercion arrow everywhere a `Submodule` term is passed to `Module.finrank`'s type-argument position.
Confirmed via a series of isolated minimal reproductions before patching the real file — a useful
debugging discipline for any future "bizarre typeclass search failure buried inside a seemingly
correct term" error.

## §2368 — `P_2KL_hasDerivAt_node` (P2KLDerivAtNode.lean, theorem 208) — THE DERIVATIVE FACT EQ (7.13) NEEDS

Search-before-build: grepped for `P_2KL_hasDerivAt`/`P_2KL_deriv` — fresh.

`P_2KL_hasDerivAt_node (K) (L) (m) : HasDerivAt (P_2KL K L) (∏_{j≠m}(ν_m−ν_j)) ν_m` — the exact
derivative fact Eq (7.13)'s coefficient formula `c^{off}_{n,2K,L} := Q^{off}_K(ν_{n,L})/P'_{2K,L}
(ν_{n,L})` needs. Proof: `HasDerivAt.finsetProd` (Mathlib's finite-product Leibniz-rule derivative,
found under its CURRENT non-deprecated name — an older `.finset_prod` alias exists but is marked
`@[deprecated]`) differentiates the product termwise, producing a sum over all indices `n` of
`(∏_{j∈erase n} factor_j(x)) • (deriv of factor_n)`; then `Finset.sum_eq_single m` collapses this
sum, since every term with `n≠m` contains the vanishing factor `(ν_m−ν_m)=0` inside its product
(because `m ∈ univ.erase n` whenever `n≠m`), leaving only the `n=m` term, `∏_{j≠m}(ν_m−ν_j) • 1`.

Three real rounds: (1) an initial `hzero` sub-proof left a trivial `x−x=0`-shape goal unsolved after
`rw[hxdef]` alone — needed a trailing `ring`; (2) the sum used Mathlib's `•` (scalar multiplication)
notation, not `*`, in `HasDerivAt.finsetProd`'s actual stated conclusion — my own `hsimp` auxiliary
lemma initially used `*`, causing a `rw` pattern-match failure; fixed by restating `hsimp` with `•`
throughout to match exactly; (3) the final `exact hprod` failed on a TYPE MISMATCH between `∏ i, fun
w => f i w` (a `Finset.prod` computed AT THE FUNCTION TYPE, i.e. Pi-type pointwise multiplication —
Mathlib's own `HasDerivAt.finsetProd` states its conclusion this way) and the goal's `fun w => ∏ n,
f n w` (a lambda wrapping a scalar product) — these are DEFEQ (Pi-type `Finset.prod` unfolds
pointwise) but not syntactically identical enough for bare `exact` to unify automatically; fixed via
an explicit `funext w; rw [Finset.prod_apply]` bridging equality, `rw`-ed into `hprod` before the
final `exact`.

EXIT0, no sorries. Spot-reverified `P_2KL_eq_zero_at_node` (§2367) clean, no regressions. 354 gated
bricks. TWO HUNDRED EIGHT Shi-lane theorems total (§2161-§2368, plus §2188 = 209 total formal
results).

explicit interpolation coefficients/vector `e^{off}_{2K,L}` can be assembled — everything needed

## S2564 (2026-09-16 03:08 CDT) — ★ decisive negative result: e1 ALONE also OOMs at 28GB, redirects the redesign entirely
Isolated `e1` (h1 scaled by one product-of-3-quartics factor, everything else stripped out) into its
own standalone file to test whether the per-block split was actually cheap. It OOM'd too, climbing
past 14.5GB at 45s and hitting the wall at 28GB (`INTERNAL PANIC: out of memory`) -- this DISPROVES the
S2563 theory that the 4-way combinatorial combination was the bottleneck. A single scaled instance of
groupClearIdentity is ALSO expensive.
**Root cause identified (not yet fixed): `set` doesn't give true opacity to `ring1`.** `set X := expr`
introduces a local `let`-definition that LOOKS atomic in the tactic-state display, but Lean's `ring1`/
`linear_combination` normalizer reifies terms via defeq-unfolding during its reflection procedure --
it can still see through the `let` back to the full ν-polynomial expansion, meaning all the `set`
calls in v2 likely provided ZERO actual memory savings; the tactic was probably still re-expanding
everything from scratch regardless. This explains why e1 (theoretically the smallest possible slice)
still blew up the same way as the full thing.
**Correct fix (queued for next cycle): use `generalize` instead of `set`.** `generalize h : expr = x`
severs the definitional connection entirely -- `x` becomes a genuinely fresh, unrelated variable that
`ring1` CANNOT unfold back to its origin (only reachable via the explicit hypothesis `h`, which isn't
consulted by ring normalization unless rewritten in first). This is the real experiment for next
cycle: redo the Q1-Q4/C1-C4 abstraction with `generalize` instead of `set`, carefully keeping h1-h4
in sync via explicit `rw`.
Ulimit safety net held clean for a 4th and 5th time (12GB/18GB/28GB tests) -- zero risk to Olympus's
network throughout this entire investigation, despite 5 consecutive OOM events.

literature splits into two regimes. (A) GENERAL quaternionic matrices: no parity constraint (quaternions'

Kramers-degeneracy systems, dimensions m=2,3,4 mod 8) -- eigenvalues are FORCED to EVEN multiplicity by the
structural map itself, i.e. the exact same odd/even mismatch Deninger proved for real coefficients can
RECUR one level up, if M_sigma's natural quaternionic lift turns out to carry that kind of structural map
(which a functional-equation-symmetric object plausibly would).

## S2630 (2026-09-16 02:44 PM CDT) — naive quaternionic-Hermitian lift of M_sigma DEFINITIVELY closed (kappa always even, proven + verified); precisely relocates the genuine escape

Ran the concrete test queued in S2629: does the "obvious" quaternionic lift of M_sigma (embed its real
entries into a genuine quaternionic-Hermitian matrix, using the standard *-structure Q_ji=conj(Q_ij)) allow
an ODD kappa (needed for RH's kappa=1), or does it fall into the literature's "regime B" (structured
quaternionic systems forced to even multiplicity)?

**RESULT: definitively regime B, no exceptions possible.** A quaternionic-Hermitian matrix (A symmetric,
B/C/D antisymmetric real blocks, Q=A+Bi+Cj+Dk) embeds into a genuine complex-Hermitian 2Nx2N matrix via the
standard 2x2-block representation; verified numerically (20/20 random NxN quaternionic-Hermitian matrices,
N=5-6, arbitrary real entries) that EVERY eigenvalue appears in an exact doubled pair, hence kappa (negative
eigenvalue count) is ALWAYS EVEN -- zero exceptions, matching machine precision. This is not an artifact of
random sampling: the underlying reason is structural (the complex embedding carries an antiunitary symplectic
structure J with J^2=-1 that commutes with the Hermitian form, the same Kramers-degeneracy mechanism behind
GSE random matrix theory) -- so this holds for EVERY quaternionic-Hermitian matrix, not just tested ones,
regardless of how arithmetic/prime data would be embedded into the quaternion components.

**This CLOSES the "obvious" quaternionic escape cleanly and honestly** -- confirms in the sharpest possible
way that Regime B (forced evenness) is what any naive/direct quaternionic lift of M_sigma would hit, exactly
mirroring Deninger's original real-coefficient parity obstruction one level up, not escaping it. It does NOT
close the broader quaternionic door: Alpay-Colombo-Sabadini's actual framework works with SLICE-HYPERHOLOMORPHIC
SCHUR FUNCTIONS on reproducing-kernel Pontryagin spaces, where kappa is defined via a kernel positivity index,
NOT via diagonalizing a finite quaternionic-Hermitian matrix -- a genuinely different object that this test does
NOT rule out (regime A: general quaternionic operators without a doubling structural map). The honest, precise
open question is now: does M_sigma admit a NATURAL slice-hyperholomorphic Schur-function representation (not
